<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Net Income (Loss) Per Share</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Basic earnings per share (&#147;EPS&#148;) is determined using the weighted average number of common shares outstanding during the period.&#160; The diluted EPS calculation is determined using the weighted average number of common stock equivalents, including both common shares, stock options and performance shares, outstanding during the period.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;For purposes of computing diluted EPS, stock options with an exercise price that exceeded the average fair market value of the common stock for the period were excluded from the diluted weighted average number of common shares.&#160; In addition, common stock equivalent shares are excluded from the EPS computation if their effect is antidilutive.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Segment Reporting</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; In accordance with the criteria of SFAS No. 131, <i>&#147;Disclosures about Segments of an Enterprise and Related Information,&#148;</i> the Company operates in a single reportable segment, the steel industry.&#160; All of the products of the Company are steel products in finished or semi-finished form.&#160; Production is the standard &#147;mini mill&#148; process where electric arc furnaces are used to melt scrap and other metallics.&#160; Liquid steel is cast and cooled, then reheated for additional forming.&#160; These processes occur at different locations, but are not dissimilar.&#160; The Company markets and sells the majority of its products through its own sales organization to customers primarily in the transportation, construction, or oil and gas industries.&#160; The Company distributes product at various locations in the United States and Canada, and as appropriate, through foreign sales
agents.&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company currently has two aggregated operating divisions: the Oregon Steel Division and RMSM Division.&#160; See Note 3 to the Consolidated Financial Statements, <i>&#147;Geographic Information,&#148;</i> for additional disclosures of revenues and assets by division and geographic location.&#160; See Note 4 to the Consolidated Financial Statements, <i>&#147;Product Sales,&#148; </i>for additional disclosures of revenues by product group.&#160; </font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Shipping and Handling Cost</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;All shipping
costs billed to customers are recorded as revenue with the related cost being
recorded under cost of sales.&#160;&#160; Internal handling costs incurred to
store, move or prepare goods for shipment are classified as selling, general,
and administration expenses.&#160; For the years ended December 31, 2005, 2004
and 2003, internal handling costs were $14.2 million, $13.5 million and $12.3
million, respectively.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Reclassifications</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Certain reclassifications have been made in prior years to conform to the current year presentation.&#160; The Company has reclassified incentive compensation between cost of sales and selling, general and administrative expenses.&#160; In addition, the Company has reclassified a portion of the fixed and other asset impairment charge taken in 2003.&#160; The portion of that charge associated with the stores and operating supplies inventories has been reclassified as cost of sales. </font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The reclassifications made to prior years do not affect operating income as previously reported.&#160; </font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Recent Accounting Pronouncements</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In November 2004, the FASB issued SFAS No. 151, &#147;<i>Inventory Costs, an Amendment of ARB No. 43, Chapter 4</i>.&#148; SFAS No. 151 amends Accounting Research Bulletin 43, Chapter 4, to clarify that the abnormal amounts of idle facility expense, freight, handling costs and wasted materials (spoilage) be recognized as current period charges. It also requires that allocation of fixed production overheads to the costs of conversion be based on the normal capacity of the production facilities.&nbsp; This SFAS is effective for fiscal years beginning after June 15, 2005.&#160; The Company has applied ARB No.&nbsp;43 consistent with SFAS&nbsp;No.&nbsp;151 and does not expect any impact on its consolidated financial statements.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In December&nbsp;2004, the FASB issued SFAS No. 153, &#147;<i>Exchanges of Nonmonetary Assets, an Amendment of APB Opinion No. 29.</i>&#148;&#160; The guidance in APB Opinion No. 29, &#147;<i>Accounting for Nonmonetary Transactions</i>,&#148; is based on the principle that exchanges of nonmonetary assets should be measured based on the fair value of the assets exchanged.&nbsp; The guidance in APB Opinion No. 29, however, included certain exceptions to that principle. SFAS No. 153 amends APB Opinion No. 29 to eliminate the exception for nonmonetary exchanges of similar productive assets and replaces it with a general exception for exchanges of nonmonetary assets that do not have commercial substance. A nonmonetary exchange has commercial substance if the future cash flows of the entity are expected to change significantly as a result of the exchange.&nbsp; SFAS No. 153 is effective for nonmonetary asset
exchanges in fiscal periods beginning after June&nbsp;15, 2005.&nbsp; During the year ended December 31, 2005, the Company adopted SFAS No. 153.&#160; The statement did not have a material impact on the consolidated financial statements.</font></p>
<p  align="center">
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">37</font></p>

<div style="page-break-before:always"></div>
<PAGE>
<br>

<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In December 2004, the FASB issued SFAS No. 123R (revised 2004), &#147;<i>Share-Based Payment,</i>&#148; which is a revision of SFAS No. 123, &#147;<i>Accounting for Stock-Based Compensation.</i>&#148;&#160; SFAS No. 123R supersedes APB Opinion No. 25, &#147;<i>Accounting for Stock Issued to Employees</i>,&#148; and amends SFAS No. 95<i>,</i> &#147;<i>Statement of Cash Flows</i>.&#148;&#160; Generally, the approach in Statement No. 123R is similar to the approach described in SFAS No. 123, however, SFAS No. 123R requires all share-based payments to employees, including grants of employee stock options, to be recognized in the income statement based on their fair values. Once effective, pro forma disclosures currently provided in Note 2 to the Consolidated Financial Statements, <i>&#147;Summary of Significant Accounting Policies,&#148;</i> in lieu of recognition of stock compensation expense, will no longer
be an alternative.&#160; The Company adopted this standard on January 1, 2006.&#160; The Company has elected to use the Black-Scholes method to fair value its stock options, and beginning in 2006, will incur expense over the vesting period for all outstanding unvested stock options as well as future grants of stock options, if any.&#160; The amount of compensation expense for the Company&#146;s performance shares also differs under the new guidance, and will be less dependent on the trading price of the Company&#146;s common stock.&#160; The Company&#146;s accounting in 2006 will rely more on the fair values determined at the grant date of the awards.&#160; As seen in the Company&#146;s pro forma disclosures for stock-based compensation, the Company&#146;s 2005 compensation expense for all awards was materially consistent with the accounting under APB No. 25, however that may change in the future.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In March 2005, the
FASB issued Interpretation No.&nbsp;47, <i>&#147;Accounting for Conditional Asset
Retirement Obligations, an interpretation of FASB Statement No.&nbsp;143&#148;
(&#147;FIN 47&#148;)</i>.&#160; FIN 47 requires the recognition of a liability for
the fair value of a legally-required conditional asset retirement obligation
when incurred, if the liability&#146;s fair value can be reasonably
estimated.&#160; The interpretation also clarifies when an entity would have
sufficient information to reasonably estimate the fair value of an asset
retirement obligation.&#160; During the year ended December 31, 2005, the
Company adopted FIN 47.&#160; The interpretation did not have a material impact
on the consolidated financial statements.&#160; See Note 23 to the Consolidated
Financial Statements, <i>&#147;Conditional Asset Retirement
Obligations,&#148;</i> for further discussion.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In May 2005, the FASB issued SFAS No. 154, &#147;<i>Accounting Changes and Error Corrections,</i>&#148; which replaces APB Opinion No. 20, &#147;<i>Accounting Changes</i>&#148; and SFAS No. 3, <i>&#147;Reporting Accounting Changes in Interim Financial Statements&#148;</i> and requires the retrospective application to prior periods&#146; financial statements for changes in accounting principle, unless it is impracticable to determine either the period-specific effects or the cumulative effect of the change.&#160; The retrospective application of the change would be limited to the direct effects of the change, and indirect effects would be recognized in the period of the accounting change.&#160; The Company adopted this standard on January 1, 2006, and does not believe that it will have a material impact on the consolidated financial statements.</font></p>

<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On July 15, 2002, the Company issued $305.0 million of 10% First Mortgage Notes due 2009 (&#147;10% Notes&#148;) at a discount of 98.772% and an interest rate of 10.0%.&#160; Interest is payable on January 15 and July 15 of each year. The 10% Notes are secured by a lien on substantially all of the property, plant and equipment, and certain other assets of the Company (exclusive of CPC and OFP), excluding accounts receivable, inventory, and certain other assets.&#160; The Indenture under which the 10% Notes were issued contains restrictions (except for CPC and OFP) on new indebtedness and various types of disbursements, including dividends, based on the cumulative amount of the Company&#146;s net income, as defined.&#160; New CF&amp;I and CF&amp;I (collectively, the &#147;Guarantors&#148;) guarantee the obligations of the 10% Notes, and those guarantees are secured by a lien on substantially all of the
property, plant and equipment and certain other assets of the Guarantors, excluding accounts receivable, inventory, and certain other assets.&#160; At any time on or after July 15, 2006, the 10% Notes will be redeemable at the option of the Company, in whole or in part at a set range of redemption prices.&#160; If redeemed during the twelve month period beginning July 15, 2006 the price is 105% of the principal amount, plus accrued and unpaid interest and any liquidated damages, as defined.&#160; The redemption price adjusts to 102.5% and 100%, respectively for the two subsequent twelve month periods.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On March 29, 2000, OFP entered into a 7-year $14.0 million loan agreement for the purchase of certain processing assets and for the construction of a processing facility.&#160; Amounts outstanding under the loan agreement bear interest based on the LIBOR rate plus a margin ranging from 1.25% to 3.00%, and as of December 31, 2005, there was $6.1 million of principal outstanding of which $2.0 million was classified as current. The loan is secured by all the assets of OFP. The loan agreement contains various restrictive covenants including a minimum tangible net worth amount, a minimum debt service coverage ratio, and a specified amount of insurance coverage. Principal payments required on the loan are $0.5 million per quarter but can be accelerated for excess cash flows, as defined. Excess cash flows generated in 2004 resulted in $0.4 million of additional principal payments paid in 2005.&#160; No
accelerated payments are expected during 2006.&#160; The creditors of OFP have no recourse to the general credit of the Company.&#160; </font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On September 17, 2004, CPC entered into a ten-year loan agreement related to an undivided 50% interest as tenants in common in a warehouse under a co-tenancy agreement. CPC&#146;s share of the debt is $3.5 million. Amounts outstanding under the loan agreement bear interest at a rate of 6.57%.&#160; As of December 31, 2005, CPC&#146;s share of the principal outstanding was $3.5 million of which $42,000 was classified as current. The loan is secured by the warehouse and contains various restrictive covenants on CPC including minimum income and cash flow requirements, a minimum debt service coverage amount and limitations on incurring new or additional debt obligations other than as allowed by the loan agreement.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On March 29, 2005, the Company entered into a Letter of Credit Facility Agreement (&#147;Credit Agreement&#148;) with U.S. Bank National Association.&#160; The Credit Agreement, as amended, provides for a maximum borrowing of $35.0 million for the sole purpose of issuing letters of credit and terminates on March 29, 2006.&#160; Under the Credit Agreement, the Company agrees to pay an issuance fee of the greater of $100 or the face amount of a letter of credit multiplied by 0.125% and a fee, payable quarterly in arrears, at a rate of 0.50% per annum of the average aggregate undrawn face amount of all outstanding letters of credit during the preceding calendar quarter.&#160; The Credit Agreement is secured by restricted cash and contains certain customary covenants for credit facilities of this type, such as provisions regarding compliance with laws, taxes, and quarterly financial reporting.&#160; As of
December 31, 2005, the Company had $22.1 million of restricted cash as collateral supporting $21.0 million of letters of credit associated with the Credit Agreement.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Camrose maintains a CDN $15.0 million revolving credit facility with a Canadian bank, the proceeds of which may be used for working capital and general business purposes of Camrose.&#160; Amounts under the facility bear interest based on the Canadian prime rate.&#160; The facility is collateralized by substantially all of the assets of Camrose, and borrowings under this facility are limited to an amount equal to the sum of the product of specified advance rates and Camrose&#146;s eligible trade accounts receivable and inventories. The credit facility contains various restrictive covenants including a minimum tangible net worth amount. This facility expires in September 2006.</font></p>
<p  align="center">
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">40</font></p>

<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">At December 31, 2005, there were no restricted amounts for outstanding letters of credit.&#160; The average interest rates for the facility were 4.4% and 4.0% for the years ended December 31, 2005 and 2004, respectively.&#160; Camrose pays annual commitment fees up to 0.25% of the unused portion of the credit line.&#160; At December 31, 2005, there was no outstanding balance due under the credit facility.&#160;&#160; </font></p>

 <tr bgcolor="#cceeff">

<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>8.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Intangible Assets</b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company has proprietary technology and water rights and accounts for these as intangible assets in accordance with SFAS No. 142, <i>&#147;Goodwill and Other Intangible Assets.&#148;&#160; </i>The Company does not have any other acquired intangible assets, whether finite or indefinite lived assets, but does carry certain pension-related intangibles.</font></p>

<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The cash and cash equivalent securities are all highly liquid investments with original maturities of three months or less at the date of purchase and are carried at cost which approximates fair value.&#160; The Company intends to hold these securities until maturity.&#160; The short-term investment securities are also highly liquid investments; however, they have maturities in excess of three months at the date of purchase.&#160; The securities are considered available for sale and are carried at fair market value.&#160; The fair value of short-term debt and long-term debt, including current portion, is estimated based on quoted market prices or by discounting future cash flows based on the Company&#146;s incremental borrowing rate for similar types of borrowing arrangements.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;At December 31, 2005, the Company has state tax credits of $3.9 million expiring 2006 through 2017, which are available to reduce future income taxes payable.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;At December 31,
2005, the Company has $33.0 million in federal net operating loss carryforwards
expiring in 2023.&#160; In addition, the Company has $150.2 million in state net
operating loss carryforwards expiring in 2011 through 2024 and alternative
minimum tax credits of $25.3 million which do not expire.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company maintained a valuation allowance of $4.0 million and $8.0 million at December 31, 2005 and 2004,&#160; respectively.&#160; The valuation allowance for deferred tax assets at December 31, 2005 consisted solely of State of Colorado net operating losses and credits.&#160; The valuation allowances at December 31, 2004 consisted of federal and state net operating loss carryforwards, alternative minimum tax credits and state tax credit carryforwards.&#160; SFAS No. 109, &#147;<i>Accounting for Income Taxes</i>,&#148; requires that tax benefits for federal and state net operating loss carryforwards, state tax credits and alternative minimum tax credits each be recorded as an asset to the extent that management assesses the utilization of such assets to be &#147;more likely than not;&#148; otherwise, a valuation allowance is required to be recorded.&#160; Based on this guidance, the Company reduced
the valuation allowance by approximately $4.0 million for the year ended December 31, 2005 due to the consistent track record of earnings throughout the year, and an update of expected future earnings including the expected profitability from the restart of the seamless pipe mill in 2006.&#160; The Company reduced the valuation by $45.4 million for the year ended December 31, 2004 due to its assessment of earnings history and the expected future reversals of net cumulative deferred tax liabilities.&#160; The Company will continue to evaluate the need for a valuation allowance in the future.&#160; Changes in estimated future taxable income and other underlying factors may lead to adjustments to the valuation allowance in the future.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company has indefinitely
reinvested approximately $22.0 million of the cumulative undistributed earnings
of its foreign subsidiary.&#160; Such earnings would be subject to United States
taxation if repatriated to the United States.&#160; The amount, if repatriated, of unrecognized
deferred tax liability associated with the undistributed earnings is not
expected to be material.&#160; </font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;During the years ended December 31, 2005 and 2004, the Company realized $2.7 million and $0.6 million, respectively, in tax benefits related to the exercise of employee stock options. The benefit was recorded to additional paid-in-capital. During the year ended December 31, 2003, the Company&#146;s tax benefits related to the exercise of employee stock options were immaterial to the Company&#146;s consolidated financial statements.</font></p>
<p  align="center">
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">43</font></p>

<br>

<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>11.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Net Income (Loss) Per Share</b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company
calculates earnings per share in accordance with SFAS No. 128, <i>&#147;Earnings
per Share.&#148;</i>&#160; SFAS No. 128 requires the presentation of
&#147;basic&#148; earnings per share and &#147;diluted&#148; earnings per share.
Basic earnings per share is computed by dividing the net income available to
common shareholders by the weighted average number of shares of common stock
outstanding. For purposes of calculating diluted earnings per share, the
denominator includes both the weighted average number of shares of common stock
outstanding and the number of dilutive common stock equivalents such as stock
options, performance shares and restricted stock awards, as determined using the
treasury stock method:</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</b>Weighted average common shares outstanding, assuming dilution, includes the incremental shares that would be issued upon the assumed exercise of stock options for the period they were outstanding.&#160; Since the average market price was in excess of the exercise price of all outstanding options, no options were excluded from the 2005 and 2004 diluted earnings per share calculation.&#160; For 2005, approximately 65,000 shares were excluded from diluted earnings per share calculation as their eventual issuance is contingent on meeting performance and market factors in the future.&#160; For 2003, approximately 595,200 shares were excluded from the diluted earnings per share calculation, as to include them would have been antidilutive considering the Company&#146;s net loss. </font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>12.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Employee Benefit Plans </b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company has noncontributory defined benefit pension plans, postretirement health care and life insurance benefit plans and supplemental retirement plans that cover nearly all of its eligible domestic employees.&#160; Certain employees are no longer eligible to participate in the defined benefit plans if they were hired after September 1, 2005.&#160; Those employees are instead enrolled in an employer funded defined contribution plan equal to three percent of annual wages.&#160; The new defined contribution plan is funded annually, and participants&#146; benefits vest after five years of service.&#160; The Company also offers qualified Thrift (401(k)) plans to all of its eligible domestic employees.<b>&#160; </b>The Company also has noncontributory defined benefit pension plans and a postretirement medical plan covering all of its eligible Camrose employees. </font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Defined Benefit Pension Plans</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The defined benefit pension plans provide benefits based on a participant&#146;s years of service and compensation.&#160; The Company funds at least the minimum annual contribution required by ERISA.&#160; The plans covering Camrose employees also provide benefits based on participants&#146; years of service and compensation.&#160; </font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On September 10, 2004, the Company finalized the labor dispute settlement (the &#147;Settlement&#148;) between the United Steelworkers of America (&#147;Union&#148;) and CF&amp;I.&#160; The Settlement included certain defined benefit pension enhancements resulting in an amendment to the plan.&#160; In addition, 200 members covered by the collective bargaining agreements accepted CF&amp;I&#146;s offer for Voluntary Early Retirement (&#147;VER&#148;), which includes unreduced pension benefits.&#160; In accordance with SFAS No. 88, &#147;<i>Employers&#146; Accounting for Settlements and Curtailments of Defined Benefit Pension Plans and for Termination Benefits</i>,&#148; special termination benefits of $6.2 million and a curtailment loss of $1.1 million were expensed in 2004 in addition to the U.S. net periodic benefit cost of $5.7 million expensed in 2004 as indicated above.&#160; See Note 17 to the
Consolidated Financial Statements, <i>&#147;Labor Matters,&#148;</i> for a description of benefits offered under the plan amendment and early retirement option.&#160;&#160; </font></p>
<p  align="center">
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">45</font></p>

<div style="page-break-before:always"></div>
<PAGE>
<br>

<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;For the U.S. plans, the accumulated benefit obligation as of December 31, 2005 and 2004 was $145.2 million and $133.4 million, respectively.&#160; The minimum employer contribution for 2005 due in 2006 is $2.9 million; however, the Company has accrued $20.1 million as a short-term liability as its estimate of involuntary and additional voluntary 2006 contributions.&#160; For the Canadian plans, the accumulated benefit obligation as of December 31, 2005 and 2004 was $25.2 million and $20.9 million, respectively. The expected employer contribution for 2006 is $1.8 million.&#160; </font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;For the U.S. and Canadian plans, assets are invested to maximize returns and minimize the risk to the participants in the plans.&#160; This strategy also involves monitoring investment portfolios to ensure appropriate diversification of assets and performance.&#160; The Company has established targeted asset allocations for the portfolios.&#160; These targets do not represent strict requirements, but are intended as general guidelines. The plans do not invest in securities of the Company. </font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Improved financial market conditions resulted in positive investment returns in the defined benefit pension plans for the years 2005 and 2004; however, plan assets continued to be lower than actuarial liabilities. The component of other comprehensive income related to additional minimum pension liability increased $3.0 million and decreased $0.1 million in 2005 and 2004, respectively.</font></p>
<p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On September 10, 2004, the Company finalized the Settlement between the Union and CF&amp;I.&#160; The Settlement included certain postretirement health benefit enhancements resulting in an amendment to the plan.&#160; In addition, 200 members covered by the collective bargaining agreements have accepted CF&amp;I&#146;s offer for VER, which includes unreduced pension benefits.&#160; In accordance with SFAS No. 106, &#147;<i>Employers Accounting for Postretirement Benefits Other Than Pensions</i>,&#148; a curtailment loss of $1.6 million was expensed in 2004 in addition to the net periodic benefit cost of $3.2 million expensed in 2004 as indicated above.&#160; See Note 17 to the Consolidated Financial Statements, <i>&#147;Labor Matters,&#148;</i> for a description of benefits offered under the plan amendment and early retirement option.&#160; </font></p>
<p  align="center">
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">47</font></p>

<div style="page-break-before:always"></div>
<PAGE>
<br>

<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The 2005 changes in Medicare regulations do not apply to the Company&#146;s postretirement medical benefits because the plan provides only a fixed benefit to retirees.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The discount rate used for the U.S. plans in determining the accumulated postretirement benefit obligation was 5.5% and 5.8% for 2005 and 2004, respectively.&#160; The Canadian plan used a discount rate of 5.5% and 6.0% for 2005 and 2004, respectively.&#160; </font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Nearly all medical benefits obligated under the Company&#146;s domestic postretirement medical plans are determined on a premium reimbursement basis.&#160; The monthly reimbursements are capped at differing amounts based on the age of the retiree.&#160; The Company&#146;s total obligation and annual expense associated with its domestic plans are substantially unchanged by variations in health care cost trend rates.&#160; The assumed health care cost trend rates used in measuring the accumulated postretirement benefit obligation for the Company&#146;s Canadian plan was 5.0% for 2005, which was assumed to remain constant at 5.0% over the next ten years.&#160; A one-percentage-point change in the assumed health care cost trend rates would have the following effect on the Company&#146;s Canadian plan:</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company has domestic profit participation plans under which it distributes quarterly to eligible employees 5% of its operating income after adjustments for certain non-operating items.&#160; The Company also distributes quarterly to eligible Camrose employees profit participation based on a sliding scale of annualized profits. Under both plans, each eligible employee receives a share of the distribution based upon the employee&#146;s base compensation in relation to the total base compensation of all eligible employees of the operating unit.&#160; In addition, the Company offers an annual incentive plan to approximately 60 senior managers</font></p>
<p  align="center">
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">48</font></p>

<div style="page-break-before:always"></div>
<PAGE>
<br>

<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">and officers based upon certain financial and operational performance criteria established for that year.&#160; Annual incentive plan participants are not eligible for distributions under the profit participation plans. The Company may modify, amend or terminate the plans, at any time, subject to the terms of various labor agreements.&#160; The Company recorded incentive compensation expense under these plans of $16.8 million, $16.0 million and $0.4 million, for the years ended December 31, 2005, 2004 and 2003, respectively.&#160;&#160; Incentive compensation expense is included within cost of sales and selling, general and administrative expenses.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company
has qualified Thrift (401(k)) plans for eligible domestic employees under which
the Company matches 50% to 100% of the first 4%, depending on the plan, of the
participants&#146; contributions.&#160; The Company&#146;s matching contribution
expense in 2005, 2004 and 2003 was $1.0 million, $0.8 million and $0.6 million,
respectively.</font></p>

<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>15.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Concentrations</b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company&#146;s Portland Mill purchases steel slab from a number of predominantly foreign producers.&#160; Any interruption or reduction in the supply of steel slab may make it difficult or impossible to satisfy customers&#146; delivery requirements, which could have a material adverse effect on the Company&#146;s results of operations.&#160; In 2005, the Company had four primary suppliers of steel slab.&#160; The Company does not maintain long-term purchasing contracts with any of its slab suppliers.&#160; Most of the steel slabs the Company purchases are delivered by ship.&#160; Any disruption to port operations, including those caused by a labor dispute or terrorism, could materially impact the supply or the cost of steel slabs, which could have a material adverse effect on the Company&#146;s production, sales levels and profitability.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>16.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Contingencies</b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Environmental </i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;All material environmental remediation liabilities for non-capital expenditures, which are probable and estimable, are recorded in the consolidated financial statements based on current technologies and current environmental standards at the time of evaluation.&#160; Adjustments are made when additional information is available that suggests different remediation methods or periods may be required and affect the total cost.&#160; The best estimate of the probable cost within a range is recorded; however, if there is no best estimate, the low end of the range is recorded and the range is disclosed.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Oregon Steel Division</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In May 2000, the Company entered into a
Voluntary Clean-up Agreement with the Oregon Department of Environmental Quality
(&#147;DEQ&#148;) committing the Company to conduct an investigation of whether,
and to what extent, past or present operations at the Company&#146;s Portland
Mill may have affected sediment quality in the Willamette River.&#160; Based on
preliminary findings, the Company is conducting a full remedial investigation
(&#147;RI&#148;), including areas of investigation throughout the Portland Mill,
and has committed to implement source control if required.&#160; The
Company&#146;s best estimate for costs of the RI study is approximately $0.5
million over the next two years.&#160; Based on the ongoing RI, limited source
control has been identified as of December 31, 2005 with an expected cost of
$0.3 million.&#160; Accordingly, the Company has accrued a liability of $0.8
million as of December 31, 2005. The Company has also recorded a $0.8 million
receivable for insurance proceeds that are expected to cover these costs because
the Company&#146;s insurer is defending this matter, subject to a standard
reservation of rights, and is paying these costs as incurred.&#160; Based upon
the results of the RI, the DEQ may require the Company to incur costs associated
with additional phases of investigation, remedial action or implementation of
source controls, which could have a material adverse effect on the
Company&#146;s results of operations because it may cause costs to exceed
available insurance or because insurance may not cover those particular
costs.&#160; It is probable that the DEQ will require the Company to perform
some stabilization of some portion of the riverbank on the Portland Mill
property; however, the Company and the DEQ have not come to terms as to the
scope of work at this time.&#160; The Company&#146;s estimate of the
stabilization costs are expected to be capital in nature and not material to the
Company&#146;s consolidated financial statements. The Company is unable at this
time to determine if the likelihood of any further unfavorable outcome or loss
is either probable or remote, or to estimate a dollar amount range for a
potential loss.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In a related matter, in December 2000, the Company received a general notice letter from the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (&#147;EPA&#148;), identifying it, along with 68 other entities, as a potentially responsible party (&#147;PRP&#148;) under the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation and Liability Act (&#147;CERCLA&#148;) with respect to contamination in a portion of the Willamette River that has been designated as the &#147;Portland Harbor Superfund Site.&#148;&nbsp; The letter advised the Company that it may be liable for costs of RI and remedial action at the Portland Harbor Superfund Site (which liability, under CERCLA, is joint and several with other PRPs) as well as for natural resource damages that may be associated with any releases of contaminants (principally at the Portland Mill site) for which the Company has liability.&nbsp; At this time, nine private and public
entities have signed an Administrative Order on Consent (&#147;AOC&#148;) to perform a remedial investigation/feasibility study (&#147;RI/FS&#148;) of the Portland Harbor Superfund Site under EPA oversight.&nbsp; The RI/FS is expected to be completed in 2008.&nbsp; Although the Company did not sign the original AOC, the Company is a member of the Lower Willamette Group, which is funding that investigation, and the Company signed a Coordination and Cooperation Agreement with the EPA that binds the Company to all terms of the AOC.&#160; As a best estimate of the Company&#146;s share of the remaining RI/FS costs, which are expected to be incurred in the next three years, the Company has accrued a liability of $1.1 million as of December 31, 2005.&nbsp; The Company has also recorded a $1.1 million receivable for insurance proceeds that are expected to cover these RI/FS costs because the Company&#146;s insurer is defending this matter, subject to a standard reservation of rights, and is paying these RI/FS
costs as incurred.&nbsp;&nbsp;At the conclusion of the RI/FS, the EPA will issue a Record of Decision setting forth any remedial action that it requires to be implemented by identified PRPs.&nbsp; The Company intends to continue to work with interested parties to assess natural resources damages. The Company estimates its financial commitment in connection with future natural resource damage assessment to be approximately $0.5 million.&#160; Based on this estimate, the Company has accrued a liability of $0.5 million as of December 31, 2005.&#160; The Company has also recorded a $0.5 million receivable for insurance proceeds that are expected to cover these costs because the Company&#146;s insurer is defending this matter, subject to a standard reservation of rights, and is paying these costs as incurred. In connection with these matters, the Company could incur additional costs associated with investigation, remedial action, natural resource damage and natural resource restoration, the costs of which
may exceed available insurance or which may not be covered by insurance, which therefore could have a material adverse effect on the Company&#146;s results of operations.&nbsp; The Company is unable to estimate a dollar amount range for any related remedial action that may be implemented by the EPA, or natural resource damages and restoration that may be sought by federal, state and tribal natural resource trustees.</font></p>

<p  align="center"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">50</font></p>

<div style="page-break-before:always"></div>

<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>RMSM Division</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In October 1995, CF&amp;I and the Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment (&#147;CDPHE&#148;) finalized a postclosure permit for hazardous waste units at the Pueblo Mill.&#160; As part of the postclosure permit requirements, CF&amp;I must conduct a corrective action program for the 82 solid waste management units (&#147;SWMU&#148;) at the facility and continue to address projects on a prioritized corrective action schedule over 30 years.&#160; The State of Colorado mandated that the schedule for corrective action could be accelerated if new data indicated a greater threat existed to the environment than was currently believed to exist.&#160; At December 31, 2005, there were 60 SWMU&#146;s that still required remediation.&#160; At December 31, 2005, the total accrued liability for all remaining SWMU&#146;s was $25.2 million, of which $23.4 million was classified as non-current on the
Company&#146;s consolidated balance sheet.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The CDPHE inspected the Pueblo Mill in 1999 for possible environmental violations, and in the fourth quarter of 1999 issued a Compliance Advisory indicating that air quality regulations had been violated, which was followed by the filing of a judicial enforcement action (&#147;Action&#148;) in the second quarter of 2000.&#160; In March 2002, CF&amp;I and CDPHE reached a settlement of the Action, which was approved by the court (the &#147;State Consent Decree&#148;).&#160; CF&amp;I has paid all penalties associated with that settlement, and was also required to convert to the new single New Source Performance Standards Subpart AAa compliant furnace.&#160; The new furnace installation was completed in the fourth quarter of 2005.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Beginning in May 2005, the CDPHE notified the Company of subsequent violations of the State Consent Decree, which included violations of opacity standards, violations of minimum intervals between tapping operations at CF&amp;I&#146;s furnaces, and failure to perform yearly relative accuracy tests for the Quality Assurance/Quality Control ultrasonic flow monitors.&#160; In October 2005, a settlement was reached between CF&amp;I and the CDPHE and included penalties for all violations with the State Consent Decree through the settlement date.&#160; The settlement provided for CF&amp;I to pay $0.2 million in penalties, fund approximately $0.8 million in supplemental environmental projects (&#147;SEP&#146;s&#148;), pay approximately $0.1 million in consulting services and make certain capital improvements expected to cost $0.7 million.&#160; At December 31, 2005, CF&amp;I paid $0.2 million, $0.3 million and
$0.1 million of the penalties, SEP&#146;s and consulting services, respectively.&#160; Other than the capital improvements, CF&amp;I accrued all unpaid settlement amounts at December 31, 2005.&#160;&#160; </font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In response to the settlement of these violations as well as other unrelated penalties, CF&amp;I expensed $0.3 million and $1.0 million during the years ended December 31, 2005 and 2004, respectively, for possible fines and non-capital related expenditures.&#160; As of December 31, 2005, the total accrued liability for all non-capital related expenditures was approximately $0.5 million.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Purchase Commitments</i></b></font></p>

<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Effective January 8, 1990, the Company entered into an agreement, which was
subsequently amended on December 7, 1990 and again on April 3, 1991, to purchase
a base amount of oxygen produced from a facility located at the Company&#146;s
Portland Mill. The oxygen facility is owned and operated by an independent third
party. The agreement expires in August 2011 and specifies that the Company will
pay a base monthly charge that is adjusted annually based upon a percentage
change in the Producer Price Index. The monthly base charge at December 31, 2005
was approximately $0.1 million. In addition, the agreement does not currently
provide benefit to the Company&#146;s operations as the Portland Mill&#146;s melt shop is
currently not in use. If the Company determines that the melt shop will not
reopen or decides to terminate the agreement, it will incur an expense for
contract termination costs. The Company estimates the cancellation and buyout
costs could range from $3.2 million to $3.8 million, depending on the
negotiation of the settlement. None of the future costs of the contract have
been accrued in accordance with SFAS No. 146, <i>&#147;Accounting for Costs Associated
with Exit or Disposal Activities,&#148;</i> as the Company has not effectively ceased its
rights under the contract.</font></p>

<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;A similar contract to
purchase oxygen for the Pueblo Mill was entered into on February 2, 1993 by
CF&amp;I, and was subsequently amended on December 15, 1994.&#160; The agreement
specifies that CF&amp;I will pay a base monthly charge that is adjusted annually
based upon a percentage change in the Producer Price Index.&#160; The monthly
base charge at December 31, 2005 was $0.1 million.&#160; The contract continues
through 2013.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company is obligated to supply a quantity of steel coil for processing through the OFP temper mill and a cut-to-length facility of not less than 15,000 tons per month.&#160; If at the end of each calendar quarter, the twelve month rolling average of steel coil actually supplied for processing is less than 15,000 tons and OFP operates at less than breakeven (as defined in the Joint Venture Agreement), then the Company is required to make a payment to OFP equal to the shortfall.&#160; At the end of each calendar year, the actual results are compared to the shortfall payment made by the Company to OFP. If the twelve month calculation results in a shortfall payment that is less than the amount paid by the Company then the Company is owed a refund for the difference.&#160; The Company&#146;s consolidated financial statements include a net charge of $0.3 million related to the shortfall for the year ended
December 31, 2005.&#160; The Company did not record similar charges during the comparable periods of 2004 or 2003.&#160;&#160; </font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In March 2005, the Company entered into an agreement to purchase the manufacturing equipment for the Company&#146;s new spiral weld large diameter line pipe mill (&#147;Spiral Weld Mill&#148;), which will be located at the Company&#146;s Portland Mill.&#160; The agreement, as amended, specifies that the Company will pay approximately $16.0 million for the delivery and installation of the machinery, which will be paid in installments as certain performance milestones are reached by the vendor.&#160; At December 31, 2005, the Company had paid $4.8 million of this commitment.&#160; The construction of the Spiral Weld Mill is expected to be completed in July of 2006.&#160; </font></p>

<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>17.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Labor Matters </b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>CF&amp;I Labor Dispute Settlement</i></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On January 15, 2004, the Company announced a tentative agreement to settle the labor dispute between the United Steelworkers of America (&#147;Union&#148;) and CF&amp;I that had been ongoing since October 1997 and on September 10, 2004 the settlement was finalized and became effective (&#147;Settlement&#148;).&#160; The Settlement resulted in the dismissal of all court actions between CF&amp;I and the Union relating to the labor dispute and environmental matters and the conditional withdrawal of charges by the United States National Labor Relations Board. The Settlement also included the ratification of new five-year collective bargaining agreements and called for the establishment of a trust.&#160; On September 10, 2004, the Rocky Mountain Steel Mills &#150; United Steelworkers of America Back Pay Trust (&#147;Trust&#148;) was established. As part of the tentative settlement the Company had originally
planned to issue four million shares of the Company&#146;s common stock to the Trust on behalf of CF&amp;I.&#160; On September 10, 2004, the parties agreed instead that the Trust would receive cash in an amount equal to the gross proceeds from the sale of four million shares of the Company&#146;s common stock in an underwritten stock offering. </font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The Settlement also included payment by CF&amp;I of: (1) a cash contribution of $2,500 for each beneficiary, a total of $2.5 million and (2) beginning on the effective date of the Settlement, a ten year profit participation obligation (&#147;Back Pay Profit Sharing Obligation&#148; or &#147;BPPSO&#148;) consisting of 25% of CF&amp;I&#146;s quarterly profit, as defined, for years 2004 and 2007 through 2013, and 30% for years 2005 and 2006, not to exceed $3.0 million per year for 2004 through 2008 and $4.0 million per year for 2009 through 2013; these cap amounts are subject to a carryforward/carryback provision described in the Settlement documents.&#160; The beneficiaries are those individuals who (1) as of October 3, 1997 were employees of CF&amp;I and represented by the Union, (2) as of December 31, 1997 had not separated, as defined, from CF&amp;I and (3) are entitled to an allocation as defined in
the Trust. The Settlement, certain elements of which are effected through the new five-year collective bargaining agreements, also includes: (1) early retirement with immediate enhanced pension benefit where CF&amp;I will offer bargaining unit employees an early retirement opportunity based on seniority until a maximum of 200 employees have accepted the offer, the benefit will include immediate and unreduced pension benefits for all years of service (including the period of the labor dispute) and for each year of service prior to March 3, 1993 (including service with predecessor companies) an additional monthly pension of $10, (2) pension credit for the period of the labor dispute whereby CF&amp;I employees who went on strike will be given pension credit for both eligibility and pension benefit determination purposes for the period beginning October 3, 1997 and ending on the latest of said employees&#146; actual return to work, termination of employment, retirement or death, (3) pension credit for
service with predecessor companies whereby for retirements after January 1, 2004, effective January 2, 2006 for each year of service prior to March 3, 1978 (including service with predecessor companies), CF&amp;I will provide an additional monthly benefit to employees of $12.50, and for retirements after January 1, 2006, effective January 2, 2008 for each year of service between March 3, 1978 and March 3, 1993 (including service with predecessor companies), CF&amp;I will provide an additional monthly benefit of $12.50, and (4) individuals who are members of the bargaining units as of October 3, 1997 and who do not choose to elect or do not qualify for early retirement, will be immediately eligible to apply for and receive qualified long-term disability (&#147;LTD&#148;) benefits on a go forward basis, notwithstanding the date of the injury or illness, service requirements or any filing deadlines. </font></p>

<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>CF&amp;I Labor Dispute Settlement &#150; Accounting</i></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company recorded charges of $31.1 million in 2003 related to the tentative Settlement obligation.&#160; The charge consisted of (1) $23.2 million for the value of four million shares of the Company&#146;s common stock valued as of December 31, 2003, (2) the cash payment of $2.5 million noted above, and (3) $5.4 million accrual for the LTD benefits noted above.&#160; As noted above, on September 10, 2004, the parties agreed that the Trust would receive cash in an amount equal to the gross proceeds from the sale of four million shares of the Company&#146;s common stock in an underwritten stock offering.&#160; On September 29, 2004, the public offering price was established at $16.00 per share, and $64.0 million was paid to the Trust in the fourth quarter of 2004.&#160; In 2004, the Company recorded a charge of $45.4 million related to the Settlement obligation consisting of (1) $40.8 million for the
incremental change in value of the four million shares of the Company&#146;s common stock, (2) $8.9 million in retirement benefits for the 200 employees who accepted the early retirement benefits, which were partially offset by (3) a reduction of $4.3 million of the existing LTD accrual.&#160; At December 31, 2004, $1.1 million was accrued for LTD benefits.&#160; In 2005, the Company recorded a reduction of $0.7 million to the LTD accrual, which was also classified as labor dispute settlement charges on the Company&#146;s consolidated statement of operations.&#160; Members of the bargaining unit who did not elect to early retire had until September 2005 to claim LTD benefits.&#160; In 2005 the Company reduced the LTD accrual established in 2004 to the expected benefit obligation for specific beneficiaries identified in September 2005.&#160; The Company expensed $2.8 million and $6.8 million during the years ended December 31, 2005 and 2004, respectively, for the BPPSO and related payroll taxes.&#160;
The BPPSO charges were classified as selling, general and administrative expenses.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>18.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Asset Impairments </b></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In July 2004, the Company idled its Napa Mill and in December 2004, the Company announced the permanent closure of the Napa Mill at which point it engaged with third parties to market the pipe mill equipment and real estate.&#160;&#160; As discussed in Note 21 to the Consolidated Financial Statements, <i>&#147;Assets Held for Sale,&#148;</i> the real estate was sold in December 2005.&#160;&#160; As a result of the sale of the real estate, at which point in time there was no prospective buyers for the equipment, as well as other factors, the Company recorded a pre-tax impairment charge to earnings of $13.7 million in 2005.&#160; In addition, the Company recorded a charge to cost of sales of $1.5 million which related to the reduction of the dedicated stores and operating supplies to net realizable value.&#160; The fair values of the equipment and the stores and operating supplies were based on quotes
from third parties. </font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In May 2003, the Company shut down its Portland Mill melt shop. The determination to close the melt shop was based on the Company&#146;s ability to obtain steel slab through purchases from suppliers on the open market, and the high energy and raw material costs and the yield losses associated with the inefficient casting technology in use at the Portland Mill.&#160; The Company continues to maintain the melt shop in operating condition.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In connection with
the melt shop closure, the Company has determined the value of the related
assets to be impaired.&#160; Accordingly, in the second quarter of 2003, the
Company recorded a pre-tax impairment charge to earnings of $18.6 million for
the melt shop and other related assets. In addition, the Company recorded a
charge to cost of sales for $8.4 million which pertained to the reduction of
dedicated stores and operating supplies to net realizable value.&#160; At
December 31, 2005, the carrying value of the fixed assets was approximately $1.3
million. The fair value of the impaired fixed assets was determined using the
Company&#146;s estimate of market prices for similar assets.&#160;  </font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;As discussed in Note 16 to the Consolidated Financial Statements, <i>&#147;Contingencies,&#148;</i> part of the settlement with the CDPHE and the EPA required CF&amp;I to install a new electric arc furnace, replacing the two former furnaces with a combined melting and casting capacity of approximately 1.1 million tons through two continuous casters.&#160; As the new single furnace operation would not have the capacity to support a two caster operation, CF&amp;I determined that one caster and other related assets had no future service potential.&#160; Accordingly, in the second quarter of 2003, the Company recorded a pre-tax impairment charge to earnings of $8.2 million for fixed assets and a charge to cost of sales for $0.9 million which pertained to the reduction of related stores items to net realizable value. Because it is believed the caster has no salvage value following the impairment charge, the
carrying value of the fixed assets was zero after the effect of the impairment charge.</font></p>

<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>19.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Capital Stock</b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Stock Offering</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On October 5, 2004, the Company received funds related to the completed underwritten offering of 8,625,000 shares of common stock at a price to the public of $16.00 per share, which included the underwriters&#146; over allotment option of 1,125,000 shares.&#160; After deducting the underwriting discount of $7.2 million and other expenses of $0.7 million, the net proceeds received from the offering were $130.1 million.&#160; Also, on October 5, 2004, the Company paid $64.0 million of the proceeds to the Trust as part of the labor dispute settlement of CF&amp;I.&#160; See Note 17 to the Consolidated Financial Statements, <i>&#147;Labor Matters,&#148;</i> for additional details.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Stockholder Rights Plan</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company has issued preferred stock purchase rights (&#147;Rights&#148;) to its common stockholders.&#160; The Rights generally become exercisable after a person or group announces a tender offer that would result in that person or group owning 15% or more of the Company&#146;s common stock.&#160; In that event, a holder will be entitled to buy from the Company a unit consisting of one one-thousandth of a share of participating preferred stock of the Company at a purchase price of $42.&#160; The Rights also become exercisable after a person or group acquires 15% or more of the Company&#146;s outstanding common stock.&#160; In that event, each Right, excluding those held by the acquirer, would become exercisable for preferred stock of the Company having a market value equal to twice the exercise price of the Right.&#160; Alternatively, if the Company is acquired in a merger or other business
combination, each Right, excluding those held by the acquirer, would be exercisable for common stock of the acquirer having a market value equal to twice the exercise price of the Right.&#160; The Company may redeem the Rights prior to a change in control at a price of $.001 per Right.&#160; The Rights will expire December 22, 2009 if not exercised prior to that date.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Stock Options</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company maintains a Non-Qualified Stock Option Plan (&#147;Plan&#148;), effective January 1, 2000. As of December 31, 2005, the Company has granted options to purchase 923,000 shares to certain senior management employees under the provisions of the Plan.&#160; The exercise price is the fair value per share on the date of grant.&#160; The term of each option is 10 years from grant date.&#160; Depending upon the particular grant, options vest under one of two schedules: 1) One-half of the options granted vest immediately upon the grant, and the remaining one-half vest ratably over a three-year period or, 2) options vest ratably over a three-year period starting with the first year anniversary after the grant date. At December 31, 2005, there were 77,000 shares reserved for future issuance under the Plan.&#160; </font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company also maintains a Non-Employee Director Stock Option Plan (&#147;Director Plan&#148;), effective April 26, 2002.&#160; As of December 31, 2005, the Company has granted options to purchase 60,000 shares of its common stock to individuals who are Non-Employee Directors under the provisions of the Director Plan at fair market value on the date of the grant.&#160; Options vest over a three year annual graded schedule from their grant date and expire no later than ten years from the date of the grant.&#160; At December 31, 2005, there were 90,000 shares reserved for future issuance under the Director Plan.</font></p>

<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Other Awards</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In 2005, the
Company issued performance awards to its employees under its LTIP.&#160; The
performance awards are earned based on the Company achieving goals within
defined performance categories over a three-year period beginning from the
January 1, 2005 service date.&#160; One half of the total performance awards are
earned based on both the market condition and performance condition, which are
not interdependent.&#160; Earned awards will be paid 60% in cash and 40% in
Company common stock.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In accordance
with APB No.25, the Company recorded compensation expense of $2.0 million in
2005 based on the quoted market price of the Company&#146;s stock at December
31, 2005 and the number of shares expected to vest.&#160; Should the Company
achieve the highest goals established for both the performance and market
conditions, the Company&#146;s share-settled obligation would be approximately
83,000 shares.&#160; There is no exercise price associated with the performance
awards.&#160; Pursuant to FAS No.123, the grant date fair value of the awards
that are earned under the performance condition is equal to their grant date
intrinsic value of $15.08 per share.&#160; The grant date fair value of the
awards that are earned under the market condition is approximately $0.5 million, and was
determined by a independent third party using simulation analysis known as the
Monte Carlo model using the following assumptions:&#160; (1) an annualized
dividend yield of 0%, (2) historic volatility of 71.0%, (3) a 3.7% risk-free
rate of return and (4) an expected award term of 3 years.&#160;
The cash-settled performance award will
be paid at an amount equal to the closing price of the Company&#146;s stock on
the last day of the three year service period.&#160; The grant date fair value
for these cash-settled awards is remeasured to fair value at each future
reporting date.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, the Company granted approximately 13,000 shares of restricted stock to its non-employee directors.&#160; The share-based awards are earned by satisfying a three year service period from the April 28, 2005 grant date.&#160; The grant date fair value of the restricted stock is equal to the intrinsic value at the date of grant, or $15.08 per share.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>20.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Sales of Subsidiary&#146;s Common Stock</b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In 1994, New CF&amp;I sold a 10% equity interest to a subsidiary of Nippon Steel Corporation (&#147;Nippon&#148;).&#160; In connection with the sale, New CF&amp;I and the Company entered into a stockholders&#146; agreement with Nippon pursuant to which Nippon was granted a right to sell all, but not less than all, of its equity interest in New CF&amp;I back to New CF&amp;I at the then fair market value in certain circumstances. Those circumstances include, among other things, a change of control, as defined, in New CF&amp;I, certain changes involving the composition of the board of directors of New CF&amp;I, and the occurrence of certain other events that are within the control of New CF&amp;I or the Company.&#160; The Company also agreed not to transfer voting control of New CF&amp;I to a non-affiliate except in those circumstances where Nippon is offered the opportunity to sell its interest in New
CF&amp;I to the transferee at the same per share price obtained by the Company.&#160; New CF&amp;I retains a right of first refusal in the event that Nippon desires to transfer its interest in New CF&amp;I to a non-affiliate.&#160; During 1995, the Company sold a 3% equity interest in New CF&amp;I to the Nissho Iwai Group under substantially the same terms and conditions of the Nippon transaction.&#160; The Company believes that it is not probable that the conditions that would permit a subsidiary stock redemption will occur. </font></p>
<p  align="center">
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">55</font></p>

<div style="page-break-before:always"></div>
<PAGE>
<br>

<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In 2005, the
Company purchased the 3% interest in New CF&amp;I previously owned by Nissho
Iwai.&#160; All minority interest associated with that interest has been
eliminated from the Company&#146;s consolidated balance sheet.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>21.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Assets Held for Sale</b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In December 2005, the Company sold the Napa Mill real estate with a carrying value of $13.8 million for $39.1 million, net of applicable selling costs.&#160; Due to the terms of the sales agreement, the Company reversed the environmental reserve of $1.0 million associated with the property.&#160; The Company recognized a gain on the sale of the Napa Mill real estate of $26.3 million, which was classified as a gain on disposal of assets in the Company&#146;s consolidated statements of income.&#160;&#160; </font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>22.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Investment in Camrose Pipe Mill and Goodwill</b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On March 30, 2005, the Company, through a wholly owned subsidiary, purchased the 40 percent partnership interest in Camrose previously owned by a subsidiary of Stelco, Inc., and the Company now indirectly owns 100 percent of Camrose.&#160; The Company has recorded the acquisition in accordance with SFAS No. 141, <i>&#147;Business Combinations.&#148;</i>&#160; The purchase price, including acquisition related costs, was $18.6 million.&#160; There are no contingent payments or any other material future obligations related to the acquisition.&#160;&#160; The Company completed the purchase price allocation and recorded goodwill totaling $3.9 million in 2005.&#160; The allocation included increases to the fair value of inventory and property, plant and equipment.&#160; The Company also recorded the fair value of customer backlog specific to significant sales orders outstanding at the date of acquisition.&#160;
In addition, the Company increased deferred employee liabilities for Camrose&#146;s defined benefit and postretirement medical plans.&#160; All minority interest associated with Camrose has been eliminated from the Company&#146;s consolidated balance sheet. </font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>23.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Conditional Asset Retirement Obligations</b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The Company adopted FIN 47 in the fourth quarter of 2005 and determined obligations exist that fall under the scope of the new Interpretation.&#160; Asbestos is believed to exist in structures located at both the Portland Mill and Pueblo Mill properties.&#160; The Company has the duty to dispose of asbestos in a regulated manner, if it were to decide to undertake a facility renovation or demolition of any of the at risk structures identified.&#160; FIN 47 requires the recognition of a liability for the fair value of a legally-required conditional asset retirement obligation when incurred, if the liability&#146;s fair value can be reasonably estimated.&#160;&#160; As the Company does not intend to change the structural configuration on any of its properties in a way that would require the removal and disposal of the asbestos, the Company cannot reasonably estimate the fair value of those
activities.&#160;&#160; The Company has not recorded a liability for conditional asset retirement obligations as of December 31, 2005.</font></p>

<p  align="center"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">56</font></p>
