<br>

<p  align="center">
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>NEW CF&amp;I, INC.<br> NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>1.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Nature of Operations</b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;New CF&amp;I, Inc. and subsidiaries (&#147;New CF&amp;I&#148;) manufacture various specialty and commodity steel products at its steelmaking and finishing facilities in Pueblo, Colorado (&#147;Pueblo Mill&#148;).&#160; Principal markets are steel fabricators, railroads, and other industrial concerns, primarily in the United States west of the Mississippi River. </font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;New CF&amp;I was incorporated in the State of Delaware on May 5, 1992, as a wholly owned subsidiary of Oregon Steel Mills, Inc. (&#147;Oregon Steel&#148;).&#160; Oregon Steel now holds a 90 percent interest in New CF&amp;I.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On March 3, 1993, New CF&amp;I (1) issued 100 shares of common stock to Oregon Steel for $22.2 million in certain consideration and, (2) as the general partner, acquired for $22.2 million a 95.2% interest in a newly formed limited partnership, CF&amp;I Steel, L.P. (&#147;CF&amp;I&#148;).&#160; The remaining 4.8% interest was acquired by the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation (&#147;PBGC&#148;) as a limited partner.&#160; On October 1, 1997, Oregon Steel purchased PBGC&#146;s limited partnership interest in CF&amp;I, and subsequently sold 0.5% to the other shareholder of New CF&amp;I.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>2.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Principles of Consolidation</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The consolidated financial statements include the majority owned CF&amp;I and the Colorado and Wyoming Railway Company (&#147;C&amp;W&#148;), a wholly owned subsidiary.&#160; All significant intercompany transactions and account balances have been eliminated.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Use of Estimates</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The preparation of consolidated financial statements in conformity with generally accepted accounting principles requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities, disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the consolidated financial statements and the amounts of revenues and expenses during the reporting periods.&#160; Actual results could differ from those estimates.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Revenue Recognition</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;New CF&amp;I recognizes revenues when title passes, the earnings process is substantially complete, and New CF&amp;I is reasonably assured of the collection of the proceeds from the exchange, all of which generally occur upon shipment of New CF&amp;I&#146;s products or delivering of the product at the destination specified by the customer.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Concentrations of Credit Risk</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Financial instruments that potentially subject New CF&amp;I to concentrations of credit risk consist principally of trade receivables. New CF&amp;I believes that risk of loss on its trade receivables is reduced by ongoing credit evaluation of customer financial condition and requirements for collateral, such as letters of credit and bank guarantees.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Inventories</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;New CF&amp;I&#146;s inventory consists of raw materials, semi-finished, finished products and operating stores and supplies.&#160; At December 31, 2005, inventory was approximately $62.4 million.&#160; As of December 31, 2005 and 2004, New CF&amp;I had recorded no adjustments for lower of manufacturing cost or market (&#147;LCM&#148;) charges.&#160; Manufacturing cost is determined using the average cost method. </font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Property, Plant and Equipment</i></b></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Property, plant and equipment are stated at cost, including interest capitalized during construction of $1.0 million, $0.5 million and $0.5 million in 2005, 2004 and 2003, respectively. Depreciation is determined using principally the straight-line and the units of production methods over the estimated useful lives of the assets.&#160; The original cost of machinery, which is being depreciated using the units of production method, is approximately $35.0 million.&#160; Total finished goods production for the years ended 2005, 2004, and 2003 were 752,000 tons, 851,000 tons, and 894,000 tons, respectively.&#160; The estimated useful lives of most of New CF&amp;I&#146;s operating machinery and equipment are from 15 to 20 years.&#160; Maintenance and repairs are expensed as incurred and costs of improvements are capitalized.&#160; Major maintenance and repair expenses for 2005, 2004, and 2003 were $30.0
million, $28.3 million, and $28.9 million, respectively.&#160; Upon disposal, cost and accumulated depreciation are removed from the accounts and gains or losses are reflected in results of operations.</font></p>
<p  align="center">
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">62</font></p>

<div style="page-break-before:always"></div>
<PAGE>
<br>

<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Intangible Assets</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Indefinite-lived intangible assets are reviewed at least annually for impairment.&#160; Intangible assets consisted of proprietary technology, water rights and pension-related intangibles at CF&amp;I, presented at cost, net of accumulated amortization. The proprietary technology is amortized over the estimated useful life of fifteen years using the straight-line method.&#160; The water rights are considered indefinite lived and not amortized.&#160; </font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Impairment of Long-Lived Assets</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;When events or circumstances indicate the carrying value of a long-lived asset may be impaired, New CF&amp;I uses an estimate of the future undiscounted cash flows to be derived from the remaining useful life of the asset to assess whether or not the asset is recoverable. If the future undiscounted cash flows to be derived over the life of the asset do not exceed the asset&#146;s net book value, New CF&amp;I then considers estimated fair market value versus carrying value in determining any potential impairment.&#160; Impairment charges of $8.2 million were recorded in the second quarter of 2003 related to the impairment of a furnace and other assets at the Pueblo Mill, as discussed in Note 13 of New CF&amp;I&#146;s Consolidated Financial Statements, <i>&#147;Asset Impairments.&#148;</i></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Income Taxes</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Deferred income taxes are provided for temporary differences between the amount of assets and liabilities for financial and tax reporting purposes.&#160; Deferred tax assets are reduced by a valuation allowance when it is estimated to be more likely than not that some portion of the deferred tax assets will not be realized.&#160; Income taxes are allocated in accordance with a tax allocation agreement between Oregon Steel and New CF&amp;I.&#160; A consolidated tax return is filed by Oregon Steel.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Segment Reporting</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In accordance with the criteria of SFAS No. 131, <i>&#147;Disclosures about Segments of an Enterprise and Related Information&#148;</i>, New CF&amp;I operates in a single reportable segment, the steel industry.&#160; All of the products of New CF&amp;I are steel products in finished or semi-finished form.&#160; Production is the standard &#147;mini mill&#148; process where electric arc furnaces are used to melt raw material and other metallics.&#160; Liquid steel is cast and cooled, then reheated for additional forming.&#160;&#160; New CF&amp;I markets and sells the majority of its products through its own sales organization to customers primarily in the transportation, construction, or oil and gas industries.&#160; New CF&amp;I distributes product to various locations in the United States, Canada and Mexico, and as appropriate, through foreign sales agents.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;See Note 3 to New CF&amp;I&#146;s Consolidated Financial Statements, <i>&#147;Product Sales,&#148; </i>for additional disclosures of revenues by product group.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Shipping and Handling Cost</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;All shipping costs billed to customers are recorded as revenue with the related cost being recorded under cost of sales.&#160; Internal handling costs incurred to store, move, or prepare goods for shipments are classified as selling, general, and administrative expenses.&#160; For the years of 2005, 2004, and 2003, internal handling costs were $2.3 million, $2.8 million and $3.0 million, respectively.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Reclassifications</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Certain reclassifications have been made in prior years to conform to the current year presentation.&#160; New CF&amp;I has reclassified incentive compensation between cost of sales and selling, general and administrative expenses.&#160; In addition, New CF&amp;I has reclassified a portion of the fixed and other asset impairment charge taken in 2003.&#160; The portion of that charge associated with the stores and operating supplies inventories has been reclassified as cost of sales. </font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The reclassifications made to prior years do not affect operating income as previously reported.</font></p>
<p  align="center">
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">63</font></p>

<div style="page-break-before:always"></div>
<PAGE>
<br>

<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>New Accounting Pronouncements</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In November 2004, the FASB issued SFAS No. 151, &#147;<i>Inventory Costs, an Amendment of ARB No. 43, Chapter 4</i>.&#148; SFAS No. 151 amends Accounting Research Bulletin 43, Chapter 4, to clarify that the abnormal amounts of idle facility expense, freight, handling costs and wasted materials (spoilage) be recognized as current period charges. It also requires that allocation of fixed production overheads to the costs of conversion be based on the normal capacity of the production facilities.&nbsp; New CF&amp;I has applied ARB No.&nbsp;43 consistent with SFAS&nbsp;No.&nbsp;151 and does not expect any impact on its consolidated financial statements.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In December&nbsp;2004, the FASB issued SFAS No. 153, &#147;<i>Exchanges of Nonmonetary Assets, an Amendment of APB Opinion No. 29.</i>&#148;&#160; The guidance in Accounting Principles Board (&#147;APB&#148;) Opinion No. 29, &#147;<i>Accounting for Nonmonetary Transactions</i>,&#148; is based on the principle that exchanges of nonmonetary assets should be measured based on the fair value of the assets exchanged.&nbsp; The guidance in APB Opinion No. 29, however, included certain exceptions to that principle. SFAS No. 153 amends APB Opinion No. 29 to eliminate the exception for nonmonetary exchanges of similar productive assets and replaces it with a general exception for exchanges of nonmonetary assets that do not have commercial substance. A nonmonetary exchange has commercial substance if the future cash flows of the entity are expected to change significantly as a result of the exchange.&nbsp; SFAS No.
153 is effective for nonmonetary asset exchanges in fiscal periods beginning after June&nbsp;15, 2005.&nbsp; The statement did not have a material impact on the consolidated financial statements.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In March 2005, the FASB issued Interpretation No.&nbsp;47, <i>&#147;Accounting for Conditional Asset Retirement Obligations, an interpretation of FASB Statement No.&nbsp;143&#148; (&#147;FIN 47&#148;).&#160;</i> FIN 47 requires the recognition of a liability for the fair value of a legally-required conditional asset retirement obligation when incurred, if the liability&#146;s fair value can be reasonably estimated.&#160; The interpretation also clarifies when an entity would have sufficient information to reasonably estimate the fair value of an asset retirement obligation.&#160; During the year ended December 31, 2005, New CF&amp;I adopted FIN 47.&#160; The interpretation did not have a material impact on the consolidated financial statements.&#160; See Note 16 to New CF&amp;I&#146;s Consolidated Financial Statements, <i>&#147;Conditional Asset Retirement Obligations,&#148;</i> for further
discussion.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In May 2005, the FASB issued SFAS No. 154, &#147;<i>Accounting Changes and Error Corrections,</i>&#148; which replaces APB Opinion No. 20, &#147;<i>Accounting Changes</i>&#148; and SFAS No. 3, <i>&#147;Reporting Accounting Changes in Interim Financial Statements&#148;</i> and requires the retrospective application to prior periods&#146; financial statements for changes in accounting principle, unless it is impracticable to determine either the period-specific effects or the cumulative effect of the change.&#160; The retrospective application of the change would be limited to the direct effects of the change, and indirect effects would be recognized in the period of the accounting change.&#160; SFAS No. 154 is effective for fiscal years beginning after December 31, 2005.&#160; New CF&amp;I does not believe that the adoption of SFAS No. 154 will have a material impact on the consolidated financial
statements.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>6.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Debt, Financing Arrangements and Liquidity</b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Borrowing requirements for capital expenditures and working capital have been provided through three revolving loans from Oregon Steel to CF&amp;I.&#160; The loans include interest on the daily amount outstanding, paid monthly, at the rate of 10.65% per annum. The principal is due on demand or on December 31, 2007 if no demand is made.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Oregon Steel is not required to provide financing to CF&amp;I and, although the demand for repayment of the obligation is not expected before December 31, 2007, Oregon Steel may demand repayment of the loans at any time. If Oregon Steel were to demand repayment of the loans, it is not likely that CF&amp;I would be able to obtain the external financing necessary to repay the loans or to fund its capital expenditures and other cash needs and, if available, that such financing would be on terms satisfactory to CF&amp;I.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>7.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Intangible Assets</b> </font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;New CF&amp;I has proprietary technology and water rights and accounts for these intangible assets in accordance with SFAS No. 142, <i>&#147;Goodwill and Other Intangible Assets.&#148;&#160; </i>New CF&amp;I does not have any other acquired intangible assets, whether finite or indefinite lived assets, but does carry certain pension-related intangibles. </font></p>

<PAGE>
<br>

<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;At December 31, 2005 and 2004, New CF&amp;I included in accounts payable amounts due from Oregon Steel of $37,000 and $61,000, respectively, related to income taxes.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;At December 31, 2005, New CF&amp;I had state tax credits of $3.6 million related to enterprise zone credits for eligible completed capital projects, expiring 2008 through 2017.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;At December 31, 2005, New CF&amp;I had $151 million in federal net operating loss carryforwards expiring in 2011 through 2024.&#160; In addition, New CF&amp;I had $139.3 million in state net operating loss carryforwards expiring in 2011 through 2024.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Oregon Steel files its income tax return as part of a consolidated group, for which a formal tax allocation agreement exists.&#160; As a subsidiary of Oregon Steel, New CF&amp;I is included in the consolidated group and thus does not file a separate tax return.&#160; Under the terms of the tax allocation agreement, each subsidiary of Oregon Steel is required to compute its separate tax liability as if it had filed a separate tax return and pay such amount to Oregon Steel.&#160; Also, each subsidiary will be compensated by Oregon Steel to the extent that tax benefits generated by the subsidiary provided a benefit on a consolidated basis.&#160; The tax allocation agreement provides that subsidiary compensation will occur only when the subsidiary contributing the loss could have utilized the loss if a separate tax return had been filed by the subsidiary.&#160; Oregon Steel has no obligation to compensate a
subsidiary until the end of September following the year in which the subsidiary could have utilized the loss.&#160; On this basis, New CF&amp;I computes its stand alone tax assets and liabilities, and reflects such balances in its consolidated balance sheets.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;New CF&amp;I maintained a valuation allowance of $4.0 million and $8.0 million at December 31, 2005 and 2004, respectively.&#160; The valuation allowance at December 31, 2005 consisted solely of State of Colorado net operating losses and credits.&#160; The valuation allowances at December 31, 2004 consisted of federal and state net operating loss carryforwards, alternative minimum tax credits and state tax credit carryforwards.&#160;&#160; SFAS No. 109, &#147;<i>Accounting for Income Taxes</i>,&#148; requires that tax benefits for federal and state net operating loss carryforwards, state tax credits and alternative minimum tax credits each be recorded as an asset to the extent that management assesses the utilization of such assets to be &#147;more likely than not;&#148; otherwise, a valuation allowance is required to be recorded.&#160; Based on this guidance, Oregon Steel reduced its valuation allowance
by approximately $4.0 million for the year ended December 31, 2005 due to consistent track record of earnings throughout the year, and an update of expected future earnings including the expected profitability from the restart of the seamless pipe mill, in 2006.&#160; In 2004, Oregon Steel reduced its valuation allowance by approximately $15.0 million due to improved earnings which increased the likelihood of utilizing the deferred tax assets.&#160; New CF&amp;I will continue to reevaluate the need for a valuation allowance in the future.&#160; As part of its realizability analysis, New CF&amp;I factors in the tax situation of the entire Oregon Steel consolidated group.&#160; Changes in estimated future taxable income and other underlying factors may lead to adjustments to the valuation allowance in the future.&#160; </font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>9.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Employee Benefit Plans </b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;New CF&amp;I has noncontributory
defined benefit pension plans, postretirement health care and life insurance
benefit plans that cover nearly all of its eligible employees.&#160; Certain
management employees are no longer eligible to participate in the defined
benefit plans if they were hired after September 1, 2005.&#160; Those employees
are instead enrolled in an employer funded defined contribution plan equal to
three percent of annual wages.&#160; The new defined contribution plan is funded
annually, and participants&#146; benefits vest after five years of
service.&#160; New CF&amp;I also offers a qualified Thrift (401(k)) plan to all
of its employees.<b>&#160; </b></font></p>

<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Defined Benefit Pension Plans</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;New CF&amp;I has noncontributory defined benefit pension plans covering substantially all eligible employees.&#160; The plans provide benefits based on participants&#146; years of service and compensation.&#160; New CF&amp;I funds at least the minimum annual contribution required by ERISA.&#160; </font></p>
<p  align="center">
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">67</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On September 10, 2004, CF&amp;I finalized the labor dispute settlement (the &#147;Settlement&#148;) between the United Steelworkers of America (&#147;Union&#148;) and CF&amp;I.&#160; The Settlement included certain defined benefit pension enhancements resulting in an amendment to the plan.&#160; In addition, 200 members covered by the collective bargaining agreements have accepted CF&amp;I&#146;s offer for Voluntary Early Retirement (&#147;VER&#148;) which includes unreduced pension benefits.&#160; In accordance with SFAS No. 88, &#147;<i>Employers&#146; Accounting for Settlements and Curtailments of Defined Benefit Pension Plans and for Termination Benefits</i>,&#148; special termination benefits of $6.2 million and a curtailment loss of $1.1 million were expensed in 2004 in addition to the net period benefit cost of $4.1 million expensed in 2004 as indicated above.&#160; See Note 12 to New
CF&amp;I&#146;s Consolidated Financial Statements, <i>&#147;Labor Matters,&#148; </i>for a description of benefits offered under the plan amendment and early retirement option. </font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The accumulated benefit obligation as of December 31, 2005 and 2004 was $75.9 million and $69.1 million, respectively.&#160; The minimum employer contribution due for 2005 in 2006 is $2.9 million, however New CF&amp;I has accrued $19.4 million as a short-term liability as its estimate of involuntary and additional voluntary 2006 contributions. </font></p>
<p  align="center">
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">68</font></p>

<div style="page-break-before:always"></div>
<PAGE>
<br>

<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Assets are invested to maximize returns and minimize the risk to the participants in the plans.&#160; This strategy also involves monitoring investment portfolios to ensure appropriate diversification of assets and performance.&#160; New CF&amp;I has established targeted asset allocations for the portfolios.&#160; These targets do not represent strict requirements, but are intended as general guidelines. The plans do not invest in securities of Oregon Steel. </font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Improved financial market conditions resulted in positive investment returns in the defined benefit pension plans for the years 2005 and 2004; however, plan assets continued to be lower than actuarial liabilities.&#160; The component of other comprehensive income related to additional minimum pension liability increased $1.9 million and decreased $0.5 million in 2005 and 2004, respectively.</font></p>

<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Postretirement Health Care and Life Insurance Benefits</i></b></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;New CF&amp;I provides certain postretirement health care and life insurance benefits for substantially all of its retired employees.&#160; Employees are generally eligible for benefits upon retirement after completion of a specified number of years of service.&#160; The benefit plans are unfunded.</font></p>
<p  align="center">
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">69</font></p>

<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On September 10, 2004, CF&amp;I finalized the Settlement between the Union and CF&amp;I.&#160; The Settlement included certain postretirement health benefit enhancements resulting in an amendment to the plan.&#160; In addition, 200 members covered by the collective bargaining agreements have accepted CF&amp;I&#146;s offer for VER, which includes unreduced pension benefits.&#160; In accordance with SFAS No. 106, &#147;<i>Employers Accounting for Postretirement Benefits Other Than Pensions</i>,&#148; a curtailment loss of $1.6 million was expensed in 2004 in addition to the net periodic benefit cost of $1.7 million expensed in 2004 as indicated above.&#160; See Note 12 to New CF&amp;I&#146;s Consolidated Financial Statements, <i>&#147;Labor Matters,&#148;</i> for a description of benefits offered under the plan amendment and early retirement option.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The 2005 changes in Medicare regulations do not apply to New CF&amp;I&#146;s postretirement medical benefits because the plan provides only a fixed benefit to retirees.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The discount rate used for the plans in determining the accumulated postretirement benefit obligation was 5.5% and 5.8% for 2005 and 2004, respectively.&#160; The benefits of these plans are not subject to health care cost trend rates.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Other Employee Benefit Plans</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;New CF&amp;I has a
profit participation plan under which it distributes quarterly to eligible
employees 5% of its operating income after adjustments for certain non-operating
items.&#160; Each eligible employee receives a share of the distribution based
upon the level of the eligible employee&#146;s base compensation compared with
the total base compensation of all eligible employees.&#160; In addition, New
CF&amp;I offers an annual incentive plan to approximately 20 senior managers
and officers based upon certain financial and operational performance criteria
established for that year.&#160;Annual incentive plan participants are not
eligible for distributions under the profit participation plan. New CF&amp;I may
modify, amend or terminate the plans at any time, subject to the terms of the
various collective bargaining agreements.&#160; New CF&amp;I recorded incentive
compensation expense under these plans in 2005 and 2004 of $6.2 million and $5.1
million, respectively.&#160;&#160;&#160; </font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;New CF&amp;I has qualified Thrift (401(k)) plans for eligible employees under which New CF&amp;I matches, depending on the plan, 50% to 100% of the first 4% of the participants&#146; contributions.&#160; New CF&amp;I&#146;s matching contribution expense in 2005, 2004 and 2003 was $0.3 million, $0.1 million and $0.3 million, respectively.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>10.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Sales of Redeemable Common Stock</b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In June 1994, the Board of Directors approved an increase in New CF&amp;I&#146;s authorized $1 par value common stock from 100 to 1,000 shares.&#160; In August 1994, New CF&amp;I sold a 10% equity interest to a subsidiary of Nippon Steel Corporation (&#147;Nippon&#148;).&#160; On November 15, 1995, a 74% stock dividend was declared, increasing Oregon Steel&#146;s holding of New CF&amp;I&#146;s common stock to 174 shares. </font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In connection with the sale, New CF&amp;I and Oregon Steel entered into a stockholders&#146; agreement with Nippon pursuant to which Nippon was granted a right to sell, in certain circumstances, all, but not less than all, of its equity interest in New CF&amp;I back to New CF&amp;I at the then fair market value.&#160; Those circumstances include, among other things, a change of control, as defined, in New CF&amp;I, certain changes involving the composition of New CF&amp;I&#146;s board of directors, and the occurrence of certain other events that are within the control of New CF&amp;I or Oregon Steel.&#160; Oregon Steel also agreed not to transfer voting control of New CF&amp;I to a nonaffiliate except in those circumstances where Nippon is offered the opportunity to sell its interest in New CF&amp;I to the transferee at the same per share price obtained by Oregon Steel.&#160;&#160; New CF&amp;I retains a
right of first refusal in the event that Nippon desires to transfer its interest in New CF&amp;I to a nonaffiliate.&#160; During 1995, Oregon Steel sold a 3% equity interest in New CF&amp;I to the Nissho Iwai Group (&#147;Nissho Iwai&#148;) under substantially the same terms and conditions of the Nippon transaction.&#160; New CF&amp;I believes that it is not probable that the conditions which would permit a stock redemption will occur.&#160; In 2005, Oregon Steel purchased the 3% interest in New CF&amp;I previously owned by Nissho Iwai and now holds 180 of New CF&amp;I&#146;s outstanding shares.&#160; </font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>11.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Contingencies</b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Environmental </i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;All material environmental remediation liabilities for non-capital expenditures, which are probable and estimable, are recorded in the consolidated financial statements based on current technologies and current environmental standards at the time of evaluation.&#160; Adjustments are made when additional information is available that suggests different remediation methods or periods may be required and affect the total cost.&#160; The best estimate of the probable cost within a range is recorded; however, if there is no best estimate, the low end of the range is recorded and the range is disclosed.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In October 1995, CF&amp;I and the Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment (&#147;CDPHE&#148;) finalized a postclosure permit for hazardous waste units at CF&amp;I&#146;s mill in Pueblo, Colorado.&#160; As part of the postclosure permit requirements, CF&amp;I must conduct a corrective action program for the 82 solid waste management units (&#147;SWMU&#148;) at the facility and continue to address projects on a prioritized corrective action schedule over 30 years.&#160; The State of Colorado mandated that the schedule for corrective action could be accelerated if new data indicated a greater threat existed to the environment than was currently believed to exist.&#160; At December 31, 2005, there were 60 SWMU&#146;s that still required remediation.&#160; At December 31, 2005, the total accrued liability for all remaining SWMU&#146;s was $25.2 million, of which $23.4 million was classified as
non-current on New CF&amp;I&#146;s consolidated balance sheet.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The CDPHE inspected the Pueblo Mill in 1999 for possible environmental violations, and in the fourth quarter of 1999 issued a Compliance Advisory indicating that air quality regulations had been violated, which was followed by the filing of a judicial enforcement action (&#147;Action&#148;) in the second quarter of 2000.&#160; In March 2002, CF&amp;I and CDPHE reached a settlement of the Action, which was approved by the court (the &#147;State Consent Decree&#148;).&#160; CF&amp;I has paid all penalties associated with that settlement, and was also required to convert to the new single New Source Performance Standards Subpart AAa compliant furnace.&#160; </font></p>

<p  align="center"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">71</font></p>

<div style="page-break-before:always"></div>
<PAGE>
<br>

<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Beginning in May 2005, the CDPHE notified the Company of subsequent violations of the State Consent Decree, which included violations of opacity standards, violations of minimum intervals between tapping operations at CF&amp;I&#146;s furnaces, and failure to perform yearly relative accuracy tests for the Quality Assurance/Quality Control ultrasonic flow monitors.&#160; In October 2005, a settlement was reached between CF&amp;I and the CDPHE and included penalties for all violations with the State Consent Decree through the settlement date.&#160; The settlement provided for CF&amp;I to pay $0.2 million in penalties, fund approximately $0.8 million in supplemental environmental projects (&#147;SEP&#146;s&#148;), pay approximately $0.1 million in consulting services and make certain capital improvements expected to cost $0.7 million.&#160; At December 31, 2005, CF&amp;I paid $0.2 million, $0.3 million and
$0.1 million of the penalties, SEP&#146;s and consulting services, respectively.&#160; Other than the capital improvements, CF&amp;I accrued all unpaid settlement amounts at December 31, 2005.&#160;&#160; </font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In response to the settlement of these violations as well as other unrelated penalties, CF&amp;I expensed $0.3 million and $1.0 million during the years ended December 31, 2005 and 2004, respectively, for possible fines and non-capital related expenditures.&#160; As of December 31, 2005, the total accrued liability for all non-capital related expenditures was approximately $0.5 million.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Purchase Commitments</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;A contract to purchase oxygen for the Pueblo Mill was entered into on February 2, 1993 by CF&amp;I, and was subsequently amended on December 15, 1994.&#160; The agreement specifies that CF&amp;I will pay a base monthly charge that is adjusted annually based upon a percentage change in the Producer Price Index.&#160; The monthly base charge at December 31, 2005 was $0.1 million.</font></p>

<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Guarantees and Financing Arrangements</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On July 15, 2002, Oregon Steel issued $305.0 million of 10% First Mortgage Notes due 2009 (&#147;10% Notes&#148;) at a discount of 98.772% and an interest rate of 10.0%.&#160; Interest is payable on January 15 and July 15 of each year. The 10% Notes are secured by a lien on substantially all of the property, plant and equipment, and certain other assets of Oregon Steel, excluding accounts receivable, inventory, and certain other assets.&#160; As of December 31, 2005, Oregon Steel had outstanding $303.0 million of principal amount under the 10% Notes.&#160; The Indenture under which the 10% Notes were issued contains restrictions on new indebtedness and various types of disbursements, including dividends, based on the cumulative amount of Oregon Steel&#146;s net income, as defined.&#160; New CF&amp;I and CF&amp;I (collectively, the &#147;Guarantors&#148;) guarantee the obligations of the 10% Notes, and
those guarantees are secured by a lien on substantially all of the property, plant and equipment and certain other assets of the Guarantors, excluding accounts receivable, inventory, and certain other assets.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Other Contingencies</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;New CF&amp;I is party to various other claims, disputes, legal actions and other proceedings involving contracts, employment and various other matters.&#160; In the opinion of management, the outcome of these matters would not have a material adverse effect on the consolidated financial condition of New CF&amp;I, its results of operations, and liquidity.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>12.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Labor Matters</b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>CF&amp;I Labor Dispute Settlement</i></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On January 15, 2004, CF&amp;I announced a tentative agreement to settle the labor dispute between the United Steelworkers of America (&#147;Union&#148;) and CF&amp;I that had been ongoing since October 1997 and on September 10, 2004 the settlement was finalized and became effective (&#147;Settlement&#148;).&#160; The Settlement resulted in the dismissal of all court actions between CF&amp;I and the Union relating to the labor dispute and environmental matters and the conditional withdrawal of charges by the United States National Labor Relations Board. The Settlement also included the ratification of new five-year collective bargaining agreements and called for the establishment of a trust.&#160; On September 10, 2004, the Rocky Mountain Steel Mills &#150; United Steelworkers of America Back Pay Trust (&#147;Trust&#148;) was established. As part of the tentative settlement CF&amp;I had originally planned
to issue four million shares of Oregon Steel common stock to the Trust on behalf of CF&amp;I.&#160; On September 10, 2004, the parties agreed instead that the Trust would receive cash in an amount equal to the gross proceeds from the sale of four million shares of the Oregon Steel common stock in an underwritten stock offering. </font></p>
<p  align="center">
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">72</font></p>

<div style="page-break-before:always"></div>
<PAGE>
<br>

<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The Settlement also included payment by CF&amp;I of: (1) a cash contribution of $2,500 for each beneficiary, a total of $2.5 million and (2) beginning on the effective date of the Settlement, a ten year profit participation obligation (&#147;Back Pay Profit Sharing Obligation&#148; or &#147;BPPSO&#148;) consisting of 25% of CF&amp;I&#146;s quarterly profit, as defined, for years 2004 and 2007 through 2013, and 30% for years 2005 and 2006, not to exceed $3.0 million per year for 2004 through 2008 and $4.0 million per year for 2009 through 2013; these cap amounts are subject to a carryforward/carryback provision described in the Settlement documents.&#160; The beneficiaries are those individuals who (1) as of October 3, 1997 were employees of CF&amp;I and represented by the Union, (2) as of December 31, 1997 had not separated, as defined, from CF&amp;I and (3) are entitled to an allocation as defined in the
Trust. The Settlement, certain elements of which are effected through the new five-year collective bargaining agreements, also includes: (1) early retirement with immediate enhanced pension benefit where CF&amp;I will offer bargaining unit employees an early retirement opportunity based on seniority until a maximum of 200 employees have accepted the offer, the benefit will include immediate and unreduced pension benefits for all years of service (including the period of the labor dispute) and for each year of service prior to March 3, 1993 (including service with predecessor companies) an additional monthly pension of $10, (2) pension credit for the period of the labor dispute whereby CF&amp;I employees who went on strike will be given pension credit for both eligibility and pension benefit determination purposes for the period beginning October 3, 1997 and ending on the latest of said employees&#146; actual return to work, termination of employment, retirement or death, (3) pension credit for service
with predecessor companies whereby for retirements after January 1, 2004, effective January 2, 2006 for each year of service prior to March 3, 1978 (including service with predecessor companies), CF&amp;I will provide an additional monthly benefit to employees of $12.50, and for retirements after January 1, 2006, effective January 2, 2008 for each year of service between March 3, 1978 and March 3, 1993 (including service with predecessor companies), CF&amp;I will provide an additional monthly benefit of $12.50, and (4) individuals who are members of the bargaining units as of October 3, 1997 and who do not choose to elect or do not qualify for early retirement, will be immediately eligible to apply for and receive qualified long-term disability (&#147;LTD&#148;) benefits on a go forward basis, notwithstanding the date of the injury or illness, service requirements or any filing deadlines. </font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><i>CF&amp;I Labor Dispute Settlement &#150; Accounting</i></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;New CF&amp;I recorded charges of $31.1 million in 2003 related to the tentative Settlement obligation.&#160; The charge consisted of (1) $23.2 million for the value of four million shares of Oregon Steel&#146;s common stock valued as of December 31, 2003, (2) the cash payment of $2.5 million noted above, and (3) $5.4 million accrual for the LTD benefits noted above.&#160; As noted above, on September 10, 2004, the parties agreed that the Trust would receive cash in an amount equal to the gross proceeds from the sale of four million shares of Oregon Steel&#146;s common stock in an underwritten stock offering.&#160; On September 29, 2004, the public offering price was established at $16.00 per share, and $64.0 million was paid to the Trust in the fourth quarter of 2004.&#160; In 2004, New CF&amp;I recorded a charge of $45.4 million related to the Settlement obligation consisting of (1) $40.8 million for the
incremental change in value of the four million shares of Oregon Steel&#146;s common stock, (2) $8.9 million in retirement benefits for the 200 employees who accepted the early retirement benefits, which were partially offset by (3) a reduction of $4.3 million of the existing LTD accrual.&#160; At December 31, 2004, $1.1 million was accrued for LTD benefits.&#160; In 2005, New CF&amp;I recorded a reduction of $0.7 million to the LTD accrual, which was also classified as labor dispute settlement charges on New CF&amp;I&#146;s consolidated statement of operations.&#160; Members of the bargaining unit who did not elect to early retire had until September 2005 to claim LTD benefits.&#160; In 2005 New CF&amp;I reduced the LTD accrual established in 2004 to the expected benefit obligation for specific beneficiaries identified in September 2005.&#160; New CF&amp;I expensed $2.8 million and $6.8 million during the years ended December 31, 2005 and 2004, respectively, for the BPPSO and related payroll
taxes.&#160; The BPPSO charges were classified as selling, general and administrative expenses.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>13.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Asset Impairments</b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;As discussed in Note 11 to New CF&amp;I&#146;s Consolidated Financial Statements, <i>&#147;Contingencies,&#148;</i> part of the settlement with the CDPHE and the EPA required CF&amp;I to install a new electric arc furnace, replacing the two former furnaces with a combined melting and casting capacity of approximately 1.1 million tons through two continuous casters.&#160; As the new single furnace operation would not have the capacity to support a two caster operation, CF&amp;I determined that one caster and other related assets had no future service potential.&#160; Accordingly, in the second quarter of 2003, CF&amp;I recorded a pre-tax impairment charge to earnings of $8.2 million for fixed assets and a charge to cost of sales for $0.9 million which pertained to the reduction of related stores items to net realizable value. Because it is believed the caster has no salvage value following the impairment
charge, the carrying value of the fixed assets was zero after the effect of the impairment charge.</font></p>

<p  align="center"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">73</font></p>

<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>16.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Conditional Asset Retirement Obligations</b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;New CF&amp;I adopted FIN 47 in the fourth quarter of 2005 and determined obligations exist that fall under the scope of the new Interpretation.&#160; Asbestos is believed to exist in structures located at the Pueblo Mill.&#160; New CF&amp;I has the duty to dispose of asbestos in a regulated manner, if it were to decide to undertake a facility renovation or demolition of any of the at risk structures identified.&#160; FIN 47 requires the recognition of a liability for the fair value of a legally-required conditional asset retirement obligation when incurred, if the liability&#146;s fair value can be reasonably estimated.&#160;&#160; As New CF&amp;I does not intend to change the structural configuration on any of its properties in a way that would require the removal and disposal of the asbestos, New CF&amp;I cannot reasonably estimate the fair value of those activities.&#160;&#160; New CF&amp;I has not
recorded a liability for conditional asset retirement obligations as of December 31, 2005.</font></p>

<p  align="center"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">74</font></p>

<p  align="center">
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>CF&amp;I STEEL, L.P.<br> NOTES TO FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>1.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Nature of Operations</b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;CF&amp;I Steel, L.P. (&#147;CF&amp;I&#148;) manufactures various specialty and commodity steel products at its steelmaking and finishing facilities in Pueblo, Colorado (&#147;Pueblo Mill&#148;).&#160; Principal markets are steel fabricators, railroads, and other industrial concerns, primarily in the United States west of the Mississippi River.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On March 3, 1993, the inception date of CF&amp;I&#146;s operations, New CF&amp;I, Inc. (&#147;New CF&amp;I&#148;), a then wholly owned subsidiary of Oregon Steel Mills, Inc. (&#147;Oregon Steel&#148;), (1) issued 100 shares of common stock to Oregon Steel for $22.2 million in certain consideration and (2) as the general partner, acquired for $22.2 million a 95.2% interest in CF&amp;I. The remaining 4.8% interest was acquired by the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation (&#147;PBGC&#148;), as a limited partner, with a capital contribution of an asset valued at $1.2 million.&#160; On October 1, 1997, Oregon Steel purchased PBGC&#146;s limited partnership interest in CF&amp;I, and subsequently sold 0.5% to another shareholder in New CF&amp;I.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>2. &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Use of Estimates</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The preparation of financial statements in conformity with generally accepted accounting principles requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities, disclosure of contingent assets and liabilities at the date of the financial statements and the amounts of revenues and expenses during the reporting periods.&#160; Actual results could differ from those estimates.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Revenue Recognition</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;CF&amp;I recognizes revenues when title passes, the earnings process is substantially complete, and CF&amp;I is reasonably assured of the collection of the proceeds from the exchange, all of which generally occur upon shipment of CF&amp;I&#146;s products or delivering of the product at the destination specified by the customer.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Concentrations of Credit Risk</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Financial instruments that potentially subject CF&amp;I to concentrations of credit risk consist principally of trade receivables. CF&amp;I believes that risk of loss on its trade receivables is reduced by ongoing credit evaluation of customer financial condition and requirements for collateral, such as letters of credit and bank guarantees.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Inventory</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;CF&amp;I&#146;s inventory consists of raw materials, semi-finished, finished products and operating stores and supplies.&#160; At December 31, 2005, inventory was approximately $62.0 million. As of December 31, 2005 and 2004, CF&amp;I had recorded no adjustments for lower of manufacturing cost or market (&#147;LCM&#148;) charges.&#160; Manufacturing cost is determined using the average cost method. </font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Property, Plant and Equipment</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Property, plant and equipment are stated at cost, including interest capitalized during construction of $1.0 million, $0.5 million and $0.5 million in 2005, 2004 and 2003, respectively. Depreciation is determined using principally the straight-line and the units of production methods over the estimated useful lives of the assets.&#160; The original cost of machinery, which is being depreciated using the units of production method, is approximately $35.0 million.&#160; Total finished goods production for the years ended 2005, 2004, and 2003 were 752,000 tons, 851,000 tons, and 894,000 tons, respectively.&#160; The estimated useful lives of most of CF&amp;I&#146;s operating machinery and equipment are from 15 to 20 years.&#160; Maintenance and repairs are expensed as incurred and costs of improvements are capitalized.&#160; Major maintenance and repair expense for 2005, 2004, and 2003 were $30.0 million,
$28.3 million, and $28.9 million, respectively.&#160; Upon disposal, cost and accumulated depreciation are removed from the accounts and gains or losses are reflected in results of operations.</font></p>

<p  align="center"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">80</font></p>

<div style="page-break-before:always"></div>
<PAGE>
<br>

<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Intangible Assets</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Indefinite-lived intangible assets are reviewed at least annually for impairment.&#160;&#160; Intangible assets consisted of proprietary technology, water rights and pension-related intangibles at CF&amp;I, presented at cost, net of accumulated amortization. The proprietary technology is amortized over their estimated useful lives of fifteen years using the straight-line method.&#160; The water rights are considered indefinite lived and not amortized. &#160;</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Impairment of Long-Lived Assets</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;When events or circumstances indicate the carrying value of a long-lived asset may be impaired, CF&amp;I uses an estimate of the future undiscounted cash flows to be derived from the remaining useful life of the asset to assess whether or not the asset is recoverable. If the future undiscounted cash flows to be derived over the life of the asset do not exceed the asset&#146;s net book value, CF&amp;I then considers estimated fair market value versus carrying value in determining any potential impairment.&#160; Impairment charges of $8.2 million were recorded in the second quarter of 2003 related to the impairment of a furnace and other assets at the Pueblo Mill, as discussed in Note 11 of CF&amp;I&#146;s Financial Statements, <i>&#147;Asset Impairments.&#148;</i></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Segment Reporting</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In accordance with the criteria of SFAS No. 131, <i>&#147;Disclosures about Segments of an Enterprise and Related Information&#148;</i>, CF&amp;I operates in a single reportable segment, the steel industry.&#160; All of the products of CF&amp;I are steel products in finished or semi-finished form.&#160; Production is the standard &#147;mini mill&#148; process where electric arc furnaces are used to melt raw material and other metallics.&#160; Liquid steel is cast and cooled, then reheated for additional forming.&#160;&#160; CF&amp;I markets and sells the majority of its products through its own sales organization to customers primarily in the transportation, construction, or oil and gas industries.&#160; CF&amp;I distributes product to various locations in the United States, Canada and Mexico, and as appropriate, through foreign sales agents.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;See Note 3 to CF&amp;I&#146;s Financial Statements, <i>&#147;Product Sales,&#148; </i>for additional disclosures of revenues by product group.&#160; </font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Shipping and Handling Cost</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;All shipping costs billed to customers are recorded as revenue with the related cost being recorded under cost of sales.&#160; Internal handling costs incurred to store, move, or prepare goods for shipments are classified as selling, general, and administrative expenses.&#160; For the years of 2005, 2004, and 2003, internal handling costs were $2.3 million, $2.8 million and $3.0 million, respectively.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Reclassifications</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Certain reclassifications have been made in prior years to conform to the current year presentation.&#160; CF&amp;I has reclassified incentive compensation between cost of sales or selling, general and administrative expenses.&#160; In addition, CF&amp;I has reclassified a portion of the fixed and other asset impairment charge taken in 2003.&#160; The portion of that charge associated with the stores and operating supplies inventories has been reclassified as cost of sales. </font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The reclassifications made to prior years do not affect operating income as previously reported.&#160; </font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>New Accounting Pronouncements</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In November 2004, the FASB issued SFAS No. 151, &#147;<i>Inventory Costs, an Amendment of ARB No. 43, Chapter 4</i>.&#148; SFAS No. 151 amends Accounting Research Bulletin 43, Chapter 4, to clarify that the abnormal amounts of idle facility expense, freight, handling costs and wasted materials (spoilage) be recognized as current period charges. It also requires that allocation of fixed production overheads to the costs of conversion be based on the normal capacity of the production facilities.&nbsp; CF&amp;I has applied ARB No.&nbsp;43 consistent with SFAS&nbsp;No.&nbsp;151 and does not expect any impact on its consolidated financial statements.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In December&nbsp;2004, the FASB issued SFAS No. 153, &#147;<i>Exchanges of Nonmonetary Assets, an Amendment of APB Opinion No. 29.</i>&#148;&#160; The guidance in Accounting Principles Board (&#147;APB&#148;) Opinion No. 29, &#147;<i>Accounting for Nonmonetary Transactions</i>,&#148; is based on the principle that exchanges of nonmonetary assets should be measured based on the fair value of the assets exchanged.&nbsp; The guidance in APB Opinion No. 29, however, included certain exceptions to that principle. SFAS No. 153 amends APB Opinion No. 29 to eliminate the exception for nonmonetary exchanges of similar productive assets and replaces it with a general exception for exchanges of nonmonetary assets that do not have commercial substance. A nonmonetary exchange has commercial substance if the future cash flows of the entity are expected to change significantly as a result of the exchange.&nbsp; SFAS
No. 153 is effective for nonmonetary asset exchanges in fiscal periods beginning after June&nbsp;15, 2005.&nbsp; The statement did not have a material impact on the financial statements.</font></p>
<p  align="center">
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">81</font></p>

<div style="page-break-before:always"></div>
<PAGE>
<br>

<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
In March 2005, the FASB issued Interpretation No.&nbsp;47, <i>&#147;Accounting for
Conditional Asset Retirement Obligations, an interpretation of FASB Statement
No.&nbsp;143&#148; (&#147;FIN 47&#148;)</i>.&#160; FIN 47 requires the recognition
of a liability for the fair value of a legally-required conditional asset
retirement obligation when incurred, if the liability&#146;s fair value can be
reasonably estimated.&#160; The interpretation also clarifies when an entity
would have sufficient information to reasonably estimate the fair value of an
asset retirement obligation.&#160; During the year ended December 31, 2005,
CF&amp;I adopted FIN 47.&#160; The interpretation did not have a material impact
on the financial statements.&#160; See Note 14 to CF&amp;I&#146;s Financial
Statements, <i>&#147;Conditional Asset Retirement Obligations,&#148;</i> for
further discussion.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In May 2005, the FASB issued SFAS No. 154, &#147;<i>Accounting Changes and Error Corrections,</i>&#148; which replaces APB Opinion No. 20, &#147;<i>Accounting Changes</i>&#148; and SFAS No. 3, <i>&#147;Reporting Accounting Changes in Interim Financial Statements&#148;</i> and requires the retrospective application to prior periods&#146; financial statements for changes in accounting principle, unless it is impracticable to determine either the period-specific effects or the cumulative effect of the change.&#160; The retrospective application of the change would be limited to the direct effects of the change, and indirect effects would be recognized in the period of the accounting change.&#160; SFAS No. 154 is effective for fiscal years beginning after December 31, 2005.&#160; CF&amp;I does not believe that the adoption of SFAS No. 154 will have a material impact on the financial statements.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>6. &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Debt, Financing Arrangements and Liquidity</b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Borrowing requirements for capital expenditures and working capital have been provided through three revolving loans from Oregon Steel to CF&amp;I as well as three loans from New CF&amp;I to CF&amp;I.&#160; The Oregon Steel loans include interest on the daily amount outstanding, paid monthly, at the rate of 10.65% per annum. The principal is due on demand or on December 31, 2007 if no demand is made.&#160; The loans from New CF&amp;I includes interest on the daily amount outstanding at prime.&#160; For the year ended December 31, 2005, interest was calculated at a weighted average interest rate of 6.2%.&#160; The principal on the New CF&amp;I loan is due on demand; however, it is classified as long-term based on New CF&amp;I&#146;s intent not to demand payment in 2007.&#160; </font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;At December 31, 2005 principal payments on long-term debt are due as follows (in thousands):</font></p>
<table align="center"  border="0" style="border-collapse:collapse" cellspacing="0"  cellpadding="0"  width="80%">

 <tr bgcolor="#cceeff">
  <td width="80%" valign="bottom">
  <p style="margin-left:1em; text-indent:-1em">
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">2007</font></p>  </td>
  <td width="2%" valign="bottom">
  <p style="margin-left:1em; text-indent:-1em">
<font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>  </td>
  <td width="1%" valign="bottom">
  <p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">$</font></p>  </td>
  <td width="15%" valign="bottom">
  <p  align=right>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">309,425</font></p>  </td>
  <td width="1%" valign="bottom">
  <p>
<font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>  </td>
 </tr>
 <tr>
  <td  valign="bottom">
  <p style="margin-left:1em; text-indent:-1em"><font size="1" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;</font></p>  </td>

  <p style="margin-left:1em; text-indent:-1em">

<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Oregon Steel and New CF&amp;I are not required to provide financing to CF&amp;I and, although the demand for repayment of the obligation in full is not expected before December 31, 2007, Oregon Steel and New CF&amp;I may demand repayment of the loans at any time.&#160; If Oregon Steel and New CF&amp;I were to demand repayment of the loans, it is not likely that CF&amp;I would be able to obtain the external financing necessary to repay the loans or to fund its capital expenditures and other cash needs and, if available, that such financing would be on terms satisfactory to CF&amp;I. </font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>7. &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Intangible Assets</b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;CF&amp;I has proprietary technology and water rights and accounts for these intangible assets in accordance with SFAS No. 142, <i>&#147;Goodwill and Other Intangible Assets.&#148;&#160; </i>CF&amp;I does not have any other acquired intangible assets, whether finite or indefinite lived assets, but does carry certain pension-related intangibles. </font></p>

<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>8.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Employee Benefit Plans </b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;CF&amp;I has noncontributory defined benefit pension plans, postretirement health care and life insurance benefit plans that cover nearly all of its eligible employees.&#160; CF&amp;I&#146;s management employees are no longer eligible to participate in the defined benefit plans if they were hired after September 1, 2005.&#160; Those employees are instead enrolled in an employer funded defined contribution plan equal to three percent of annual wages.&#160; The new defined contribution plan is funded annually, and participants&#146; benefits vest after five years of service.&#160; CF&amp;I also offers a qualified Thrift (401(k)) plan to all of its employees.<b>&#160; </b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Defined Benefit Pension Plans</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;CF&amp;I has noncontributory defined benefit pension plans covering substantially all eligible employees.&#160; The plans provide benefits based on participants&#146; years of service and compensation.&#160; CF&amp;I funds at least the minimum annual contribution required by ERISA.&#160; </font></p>

<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On September 10, 2004, CF&amp;I finalized the labor dispute settlement (the &#147;Settlement&#148;) between the United Steelworkers of America (&#147;Union&#148;) and CF&amp;I.&#160; The Settlement included certain defined benefit pension enhancements resulting in an amendment to the plan.&#160; In addition, 200 members covered by the collective bargaining agreements have accepted CF&amp;I&#146;s offer for Voluntary Early Retirement (&#147;VER&#148;) which includes unreduced pension benefits.&#160; In accordance with SFAS No. 88, &#147;<i>Employers&#146; Accounting for Settlements and Curtailments of Defined Benefit Pension Plans and for Termination Benefits</i>,&#148; special termination benefits of $6.2 million and a curtailment loss of $1.1 million were expensed in 2004 in addition to the net period benefit cost of $4.1 million expensed in 2004 as indicated above.&#160; See Note 10 to CF&amp;I&#146;s
Financial Statements, <i>&#147;Labor Matters,&#148; </i>for a description of benefits offered under the plan amendment and early retirement option. </font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The accumulated benefit obligation as of December 31, 2005 and 2004 was $75.9 million and $69.1 million, respectively.&#160; The minimum employer contribution due for 2005 in 2006 is $2.9 million, however CF&amp;I has accrued $19.4 million as a short-term liability as its estimate of involuntary and additional voluntary 2006 contributions. </font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Assets are invested to maximize returns and minimize the risk to the participants in the plans.&#160; This strategy also involves monitoring investment portfolios to ensure appropriate diversification of assets and performance.&#160; CF&amp;I has established targeted asset allocations for the portfolios.&#160; These targets do not represent strict requirements, but are intended as general guidelines. The plans do not invest in securities of Oregon Steel. </font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Plan assets are invested as follows as of December 31 (defined benefit pension plans&#146; measurement date):</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Improved financial market conditions resulted in positive investment returns in the defined benefit pension plans for the years 2005 and 2004; however, plan assets continued to be lower than actuarial liabilities.&#160; The component of other comprehensive income related to additional minimum pension liability increased $1.9 million and decreased $0.9 million in 2005 and 2004, respectively.</font></p>

<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Postretirement Health Care and Life Insurance Benefits</i></b></font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;CF&amp;I provides certain postretirement health care and life insurance benefits for substantially all of its retired employees.&#160; Employees are generally eligible for benefits upon retirement after completion of a specified number of years of service.&#160; The benefit plans are unfunded.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Other Employee Benefit Plans</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;CF&amp;I has a profit participation plan under which it distributes quarterly to eligible employees 5% of its operating income after adjustments for certain non-operating items.&#160; Each eligible employee receives a share of the distribution based upon the level of the eligible employee&#146;s base compensation compared with the total base compensation of all eligible employees.&#160; In addition, CF&amp;I offers an annual incentive plan to approximately 20 senior managers and officers based upon certain financial and operational performance criteria established for that year.&#160; Annual incentive plan participants are not eligible for distributions under the profit participation plan. CF&amp;I may modify, amend or terminate the plans at any time, subject to the terms of the various collective bargaining agreements.&#160; CF&amp;I recorded incentive compensation expense under these plans in 2005 and
2004 of $6.2 million and $5.1 million, respectively.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;CF&amp;I has qualified Thrift (401(k)) plans for eligible employees under which CF&amp;I matches, depending on the plan, 50% to 100% of the first 4% of the participants&#146; contributions.&#160; CF&amp;I&#146;s matching contribution expense in 2005, 2004 and 2003 was $0.3 million, $0.1 million and $0.3 million, respectively.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b>9.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Contingencies</b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Environmental </i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;All material environmental remediation liabilities for non-capital expenditures, which are probable and estimable, are recorded in the consolidated financial statements based on current technologies and current environmental standards at the time of evaluation.&#160; Adjustments are made when additional information is available that suggests different remediation methods or periods may be required and affect the total cost.&#160; The best estimate of the probable cost within a range is recorded; however, if there is no best estimate, the low end of the range is recorded and the range is disclosed.</font></p>

<p><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In October 1995, CF&amp;I and the Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment (&#147;CDPHE&#148;) finalized a postclosure permit for hazardous waste units at CF&amp;I&#146;s mill in Pueblo, Colorado.&#160; As part of the postclosure permit requirements, CF&amp;I must conduct a corrective action program for the 82 solid waste management units (&#147;SWMU&#148;) at the facility and continue to address projects on a prioritized corrective action schedule over 30 years.&#160; The State of Colorado mandated that the schedule for corrective action could be accelerated if new data indicated a greater threat existed to the environment than was currently believed to exist.&#160; At December 31, 2005, there were 60 SWMU&#146;s that still required remediation.&#160; At December 31, 2005, the total accrued liability for all remaining SWMU&#146;s was $25.2 million, of which $23.4 million was classified as
non-current on CF&amp;I&#146;s consolidated balance sheet.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The CDPHE inspected the Pueblo Mill in 1999 for possible environmental violations, and in the fourth quarter of 1999 issued a Compliance Advisory indicating that air quality regulations had been violated, which was followed by the filing of a judicial enforcement action (&#147;Action&#148;) in the second quarter of 2000.&#160; In March 2002, CF&amp;I and CDPHE reached a settlement of the Action, which was approved by the court (the &#147;State Consent Decree&#148;).&#160; CF&amp;I has paid all penalties associated with that settlement, and was also required to convert to the new single New Source Performance Standards Subpart AAa compliant furnace.&#160; </font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Beginning in May 2005, the CDPHE notified the Company of subsequent violations of the State Consent Decree, which included violations of opacity standards, violations of minimum intervals between tapping operations at CF&amp;I&#146;s furnaces, and failure to perform yearly relative accuracy tests for the Quality Assurance/Quality Control ultrasonic flow monitors.&#160; In October 2005, a settlement was reached between CF&amp;I and the CDPHE and included penalties for all violations with the State Consent </font></p>

<p  align="center"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman">87</font></p>

<div style="page-break-before:always"></div>
<PAGE>
<br>

<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">Decree through the settlement date.&#160; The settlement provided for CF&amp;I to pay $0.2 million in penalties, fund approximately $0.8 million in supplemental environmental projects (&#147;SEP&#146;s&#148;), pay approximately $0.1 million in consulting services and make certain capital improvements expected to cost $0.7 million.&#160; At December 31, 2005, CF&amp;I paid $0.2 million, $0.3 million and $0.1 million of the penalties, SEP&#146;s and consulting services, respectively.&#160; Other than the capital improvements, CF&amp;I accrued all unpaid settlement amounts at December 31, 2005.&#160;&#160; </font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In response to the settlement of these violations as well as other unrelated penalties, CF&amp;I expensed $0.3 million and $1.0 million during the years ended December 31, 2005 and 2004, respectively, for possible fines and non-capital related expenditures.&#160; As of December 31, 2005, the total accrued liability for all non-capital related expenditures was approximately $0.5 million.</font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><b><i>Purchase Commitments</i></b></font></p>
<p>
<font size="2" face="Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;A contract to purchase oxygen for the Pueblo Mill was entered into on February 2, 1993 by CF&amp;I, and was subsequently amended on December 15, 1994.&#160; The agreement specifies that CF&amp;I will pay a base monthly charge that is adjusted annually based upon a percentage change in the Producer Price Index.&#160; The monthly base charge at December 31, 2005 was $0.1 million.</font></p>
